attrs.statement: System sends the first reminder to the provider at the reminder-timing setting (default 6 hours after the End Treatment gate is first met) if documentation is still incomplete; the second reminder follows at the configured completion deadline (default 24 hours); the admin dashboard then flags the treatment as "Overdue Documentation" for manual follow-up. Reminders and the flag stop when the case is Closed Early or blocked. Enforcement is reminders plus the flag only; nothing is blocked.
attrs.rationale: Overlaps REQ-010-010; the defaults (6 hours for the first reminder, 24 hours for the deadline) are both configurable. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 919.

nodes.title: If real-time sync fails, viewers see the last known status with a last-updated indicator

attrs.statement: If real-time sync fails, queue update for retry; patient/admin see last known day status with "last updated [time] ago" indicator
attrs.rationale: Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 752.

nodes.title: Notification failure does not block the treatment workflow

attrs.statement: If notification fails, queue for retry; notifications are informational, not critical to treatment workflow
attrs.rationale: Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 762.

nodes.title: Patient consent for photo storage and use is obtained during booking

attrs.statement: Treatment documentation must comply with HIPAA-equivalent standards (access controls, audit trails, encryption); patient consent obtained during booking for photo storage and usage
attrs.rationale: The whole Compliance line is kept because the consent clause is part of the same sentence as the HIPAA-equivalent requirement. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 784.

nodes.title: Treatment record status lifecycle

attrs.statement: status ("Awaiting Check In", "In Progress", "Completed", "Closed Early", "Cancelled"; the record is created with status "Awaiting Check In" when the booking becomes `Confirmed`, seeded from the accepted snapshot, so treatment-detail changes before Check In have a record to change; Check In sets "In Progress"; saving End Treatment sets "Completed"; "Cancelled" is set when the booking is cancelled before Check In (the FR-006 Cancel Booking action, the provider-status cascade, or the provider-fault transfer) or when an admin cancels an In Progress booking through the FR-006 Screen 11 decision after a provider fault or a provider status cascade, and the FR-030 `treatment.cancelled` event is then emitted (REQ-010-122); when an admin moves an In Progress booking to Aftercare through the FR-006 Screen 11 decision (early close, or after a provider fault or provider status cascade under FR-006 Alternative Flow B7), the record becomes "Closed Early"; in both In Progress cases the record keeps what was documented and provider documentation stays blocked; cause and `supportRequired` are held on the booking
attrs.rationale: From Key Entities, Entity 1. Overlaps Rule 2 on record creation; possible duplicate within this FR. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 986.

nodes.title: Progress summary and current day status calculated from day statuses

attrs.statement: Overall Progress: Summary of treatment completion (e.g., "2 of 3 days complete") (Display only; auto-calculated from day statuses) Days Status Summary: Completion summary e.g., "2 / 3 days complete" Current Day Status: Status of the most recent active day
attrs.rationale: Screens SCR-010-01, SCR-010-03 and SCR-010-07. How the most recent active day is chosen is not stated. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 275, 330, 331.

nodes.title: Plan day position shown as a relative position, never a calendar date

attrs.statement: Plan Day Position: Relative position of this day in the treatment plan (e.g., "Day 2 of 4") (Display only; relative day number only, never converted to or shown as a calendar date)
attrs.rationale: Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 298.

nodes.title: Provider In Progress listing: own clinic only, live search and filters, sorted by procedure date

attrs.statement: List shows only cases in "In Progress" status for the provider's clinic. Search and filters apply in real-time without page reload. Clicking a row (the Patient ID) opens Screen 4: In Progress Case Detail. Default sort: procedure date ascending.
attrs.rationale: Screen SCR-010-03. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 335, 337, 338.

nodes.title: Admin listing: all providers' cases by status and flag, opens the case in editable mode

attrs.statement: Admin listing shows all providers' cases in the selected case status (default In Progress), with a flag filter and a Flags column — platform-wide visibility. Clicking a row or the Action button opens Screen 8: In Progress Case Detail in editable mode, whatever the case status; the controls shown follow the status. Default sort: procedure date ascending.
attrs.rationale: Screen SCR-010-07. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 472, 473, 474.

nodes.title: End Treatment enabled when every day is terminal, at least one day is finished, and the case is not on hold

attrs.statement: End Treatment is enabled only when every day record is in a terminal status (Finished, Need caution/attention, or Cancelled/Deferred), at least one day is Finished or Need caution/attention, and the booking carries no `supportRequired` marker; a case with every day Cancelled/Deferred goes to the early close (Rule 17); a partly delivered treatment (at least one day Finished, the others Cancelled/Deferred) ends with End Treatment and needs no close request; the documentation deadline starts when the gate is first met
attrs.rationale: Screens SCR-010-04 and SCR-010-06. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 386, 438.

nodes.title: Provider may reopen Day Edit at any time while the case is In Progress

attrs.statement: Provider may return to this modal at any time while the case is In Progress.
attrs.rationale: Screen SCR-010-05. Archived FR-010 PRD baseline, lines 413.

nodes.title: Check In allowed only when Confirmed, procedure date reached, fully paid, not on hold, and no other case In Progress

attrs.statement: System MUST allow Check In only when the booking is Confirmed, the procedure date is today or in the past in the appointment timezone, the booking is fully paid with no Defaulted installment, it has no `supportRequired` marker, and the patient has no other treatment In Progress; otherwise Check In is disabled and a generic reason is shown to the provider. This is the one merged Check In rule (Rule 3; Payment Rule 2)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-04. Merges the former FR-006 Check In rule.

nodes.title: Report Issue Before Check In control for No-show and Medical postponement; flags the case for the admin only

attrs.statement: System MUST give providers a Report Issue Before Check In control on a Confirmed case, with the reasons No-show and Medical postponement, that only flags the case for the admin and leaves the booking Confirmed; Cancel / Close Case remains available only while the case is In Progress, with the Alternative Flow B4 reason list (Alternative Flows B1, B2 and B4; Screen 4)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-04. Alternative Flows B1, B2 and B4.

nodes.title: Provider In Progress listing filters by treatment start date range

attrs.statement: System MUST let providers filter the In Progress listing by treatment start date range, defaulting to the current month (Screen 3)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-03.

nodes.title: Provider In Progress listing filters by assigned clinician

attrs.statement: System MUST let providers filter the In Progress listing by any assigned clinician, chosen from the clinic's active clinicians (Screen 3)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-03.

nodes.title: Admin In Progress listing filters by provider or clinic

attrs.statement: System MUST let admins filter the admin In Progress listing by provider or clinic (Screen 7)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-07.

nodes.title: Admin In Progress listing filters by procedure start date range

attrs.statement: System MUST let admins filter the admin In Progress listing by procedure start date range, defaulting to the current month (Screen 7)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-07.

nodes.title: Admin In Progress listing filters by assigned clinician

attrs.statement: System MUST let admins filter the admin In Progress listing by any assigned clinician (Screen 7)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-07.

nodes.title: Case detail page in tabs; the In Progress tab becomes active at Check In

attrs.statement: System MUST present the provider case detail page in tabs (Treatment Plan, Note, Book hotel & Book flight, In Progress); the In Progress tab becomes the active tab at Check In and the other tabs stay accessible for reference (Screen 4)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Screen SCR-010-04.

nodes.title: Admin In Progress listing search by patient ID, name, booking reference or provider name

attrs.statement: System MUST let admins search the admin In Progress listing by patient ID, patient name, booking reference or provider name, with the results filtering in real time (Screen 7)
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 459 (Screen 7 Search Bar: patient ID, name, booking reference, or provider name; real-time filter)

nodes.title: Admin notices from FR-010 are dashboard flags, not FR-030 events

attrs.statement: System MUST show the admin notices raised by FR-010 (report issue before Check In, close request, Late Check In, Overdue Documentation, failed completion signal) as dashboard flags in the Flags column of the admin case listing and on the case detail, not FR-030 events; the action on a failed completion signal is a retry (Rule 18)
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, Rule 18. No FR-030 event exists for these notices.

nodes.title: Early close of an In Progress case without a fault: payout eligible on the decision date, record becomes Closed Early

attrs.statement: System MUST let an admin close an In Progress case early on FR-006 Screen 11 when the provider is not at fault, make the provider's share eligible for payout on the decision date after the refund and commission with no waiting window, set the treatment record to Closed Early, stop reminders and the Overdue Documentation flag, signal FR-011 so the aftercare team writes the post-op instructions, and never have the admin fill the End of Treatment fields (Rule 17; Alternative Flow B4)
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, Rule 17. FR-006 owns the decision screen; the FR-010 side is the record status, the reminders, and the payout trigger. The refund comes out of what the patient paid.

nodes.title: End Treatment save marks completion, moves the booking to Aftercare under FR-006, and starts the confirmation window

attrs.statement: System MUST mark the treatment Completed at End Treatment save, have FR-006 move the booking to Aftercare in the same step whether or not the FR-011 signal is delivered, and start the FR-007 patient confirmation window at that moment; the save and the booking move succeed or fail together, and a save is rejected when the case gains the `supportRequired` marker meanwhile (Integration 5)
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, Integration 5. FR-006 owns the booking status change; FR-007 owns the confirmation window.

nodes.title: Late Check In after the appointment date needs a provider confirmation and shows an admin flag

attrs.statement: System MUST allow Check In after the appointment date with no upper limit, require the provider to confirm a late Check In prompt, and show the admin a Late Check In flag (Alternative Flow A3)
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A3. Dates are compared in the booking's appointment timezone.

nodes.title: An admin may record a provider fault from Screen 8 without the provider withdrawing

attrs.statement: System MUST let an admin record a provider fault from Screen 8 without the provider withdrawing, with a mandatory audited reason, setting the `supportRequired` marker with cause ProviderFault and opening the FR-006 provider-fault action (Alternative Flow B6)
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B6. FR-006 owns the provider-fault decision screens.

nodes.title: The supportRequired marker blocks documentation and every End Treatment

attrs.statement: System MUST block provider documentation and every End Treatment, the admin button included, on any In Progress case with the `supportRequired` marker, whatever the cause, and stop reminders and the Overdue Documentation flag (Rule 12)
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, Rule 12.

nodes.title: Admin case listing has a status filter, a flag filter and a Flags column; Screen 8 opens for any status; failed signal has a Retry button

attrs.statement: System MUST give admins a case listing (Screen 7) with a case status filter (default In Progress), a flag filter, and a Flags column, MUST open Screen 8 from it for a case in any status, and MUST show a Retry Completion Signal button on Screen 8 while the failed-signal flag is set (Rule 18)
attrs.rationale: Screens 7 and 8, Rule 18. A failed-signal case is already in Aftercare, so it is found through the status filter.

nodes.title: treatment.cancelled is emitted when the treatment record becomes Cancelled

attrs.statement: System MUST emit the FR-030 `treatment.cancelled` event when the treatment record becomes Cancelled: a booking cancelled before Check In, the provider-fault transfer, or an In Progress booking cancelled by an admin through the FR-006 Screen 11 decision (Entity 1)
attrs.rationale: Entity 1 and Integration 3. The event is already emitted at STG-main-06-treatment; this rule names the FR-010 routes that fire it.

nodes.title: A team member who leaves the case is replaced in the clinician set of open treatment records

attrs.statement: System MUST, when a team member is removed or suspended, has a role change that takes away the rights needed to work their open items, or is force-suspended or force-removed by an admin, rewrite the clinician set (clinician_ids) of every open treatment record (Awaiting Check In or In Progress) that names the member to the replacement clinician chosen at that moment, as a system change recorded in the treatment record's audit history and not as a treatment-detail change (Alternative Flow A2); the other clinicians on the record stay and at least one remains; Completed, Closed Early and Cancelled records keep their clinician set; reactivating the member does not give the records back (FR-009 REQ-009-191)

nodes.title: Treatment-linked and standalone activation paths

attrs.statement: System MUST support treatment-linked and standalone aftercare activation paths; a standalone request may also start as a conversion from FR-038 monitoring (REQ-011-093)

nodes.title: Patients complete milestone tasks with reminders and quality validation

attrs.statement: Patients MUST be able to complete milestone tasks (scan uploads, questionnaires) with reminders and quality validation
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 1610 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Providers configure and activate plans from templates

attrs.statement: Providers MUST be able to configure and activate aftercare plans with template customization
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 1611 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Admin oversees cases, reassigns and overrides plans with audit

attrs.statement: Admin MUST be able to oversee cases, reassign providers, and override plans with full audit. Admin assignment of who delivers the aftercare (a provider, whose clinic staff are the aftercare specialists, or a Hairline aftercare team member, an admin with the FR-031 Aftercare Coordinator role) is owned by FR-011. The Aftercare Coordinator works on the admin aftercare Screens 13 to 19 (plan configuration, scan review, escalations) when the Hairline team delivers.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 1612 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Milestones, tasks, progress and adherence tracked as entities

attrs.statement: System MUST track milestones, tasks, progress, and adherence as structured entities
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 1619 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Aftercare artifacts retained per retention policy

attrs.statement: System MUST retain all aftercare artifacts (scans, questionnaires, communications) per retention policy
attrs.rationale: Retention periods follow the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period (Data and Privacy Rule 1).

nodes.title: Progress derived deterministically

attrs.statement: Progress MUST be derived deterministically from plan and task completion (completed scan, questionnaire and education tasks over total such tasks; medication adherence is tracked separately)
attrs.rationale: The formula is stated in Milestone and Task Rule 3, on Screen 1 and in Workflow 3 step 4.

nodes.title: Provider sees patient details from assignment (standalone) or payment (add-on)

attrs.statement: The assigned provider MUST see patient details from assignment in the standalone flow, and from payment in the post-treatment add-on flow, where assignment follows payment; the admin is exempt and always sees them.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 3 and Data and Privacy Rule 2; access from assignment follows REQ-038-050.

nodes.title: Media stored in secure storage with controlled access

attrs.statement: System MUST store media artifacts in secure storage with controlled access
attrs.rationale: Restated by Data and Privacy Rule 3 (scan media stored securely with access controls).

nodes.title: Questionnaires referenced from FR-025

attrs.statement: System MUST reference questionnaires managed in FR-025 for aftercare context
attrs.rationale: Restated on Screens 3, 10 and 16; content ownership stays with FR-025.

nodes.title: Provider suspension or deactivation does not cancel standalone aftercare

attrs.statement: When a provider's suspension or deactivation becomes effective, System MUST NOT cancel that provider's non-terminal standalone aftercare cases; it MUST record cause `ProviderSuspended` or `ProviderDeactivated` and an independent `supportRequired` marker and route them to Screen 19 reassignment (treatment-linked cases follow REQ-011-015), retain the completion milestone and aftercare records, and route recovery continuity to admins for resolution through the existing reassignment/recovery workflow, without automatic reassignment or restoration on reactivation (Workflow 4 D4; FR-015 A5/Screen 4)
attrs.rationale: Restated by Workflow 4 D4, General Module Rule 4 and the mid-aftercare suspension edge case. The treatment-linked behaviour is stated in D4 and Rule 4 and recorded as its own Rule.

nodes.title: Admin reassigns aftercare provider or team on Screen 19

attrs.statement: System MUST let an admin reassign the aftercare provider or team on Screen 19 with a mandatory reason, confirmation, audit entry, and the `aftercare.provider_reassigned` notice (recipients, content, and the mandatory status of the notice are defined by the FR-030 notification Rules REQ-030-026 and REQ-030-077); for a treatment-linked case the booking MUST stay `Aftercare` and the treatment record MUST stay unchanged, with no new quote, acceptance, or payment
attrs.rationale: Restated by Workflow 4 D5 and the Screen 19 business rules.

nodes.title: Aftercare has exactly three entry sources

attrs.statement: Aftercare has exactly three entry sources: treatment-linked aftercare (starts from the patient's accepted Hairline quote whose treatment was performed, covering the Workflow 1 setup and the Workflow 2b post-treatment add-on bought within 90 days), standalone aftercare (bought directly by patients treated at an outside clinic, with no inquiry or quote), and standalone aftercare converted from an FR-038 monitoring case (a standalone request with the monitoring data pre-filled, REQ-011-093). Admin assignment is a step inside these routes, not a separate route.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points, prd.md line 64 onward.

nodes.title: Treatment-linked setup starts automatically at treatment completion

attrs.statement: Treatment-linked aftercare setup starts automatically at treatment completion, on the FR-010 completion signal. The plan activates when the provider confirms it (REQ-011-055) or an admin activates it (REQ-011-019). FR-006 owns the move of the booking to Aftercare.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 1. Workflow 1 step 1: the provider marks the treatment completed, the system moves the patient status to Aftercare and prompts the provider to configure the aftercare plan. The booking transition itself is owned by FR-006.

nodes.title: Standalone aftercare requires payment before activation

attrs.statement: Standalone aftercare requires payment before activation: payment activates the service and, for a standalone request, comes last, after the admin has assigned a provider and the provider has configured the plan. A post-treatment add-on pays before automatic assignment.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 1; Payment Rules 1 and 4 (payment timing); Workflow 2.

nodes.title: Admin can manually activate aftercare for special cases

attrs.statement: Admin can manually activate aftercare for special cases, including a plan whose setup stays unconfirmed after the escalation of REQ-011-090. Manual activation needs a mandatory reason and creates an audit entry.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 1.

nodes.title: Standard duration 6-12 months, extensions proposed by the provider or coordinator and approved by the admin

attrs.statement: Standard aftercare duration is 6-12 months, determined by treatment type and complexity. Extensions are proposed by the provider (or the coordinator) with a reason and approved or rejected by the admin (REQ-011-098).
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 2.

nodes.title: Data access limited by role: own, assigned, all

attrs.statement: Patients can only access their own aftercare data. Providers can only access assigned patients. Admin has full access to all aftercare data.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 3 and Data Access Rule 2; repeated on Screens 8, 9 and 12 (provider sees only assigned patients).

nodes.title: Milestones progress by time, cannot be skipped and close on schedule; a required task not done by then is Missed

attrs.statement: Milestones progress automatically based on time elapsed and close on schedule at their end. Patients cannot skip milestones. A required scan, questionnaire or education task not done by the milestone end becomes Missed (task status missed), and the plan completes at the end of the last milestone (REQ-011-096). Medication tick-offs are adherence tracking only and do not affect a milestone.
attrs.rationale: Milestone and Task Rule 1.

nodes.title: Task completion standards

attrs.statement: Scan uploads must meet the quality threshold. Questionnaires must be completed in full. Medication adherence is tracked but has no effect on a milestone and is not part of the progress percentage.
attrs.rationale: Milestone and Task Rule 2; Screen 2 (minimum quality threshold) and Screen 3 (all required fields) business rules.

nodes.title: Overdue tasks escalate after 48 hours

attrs.statement: Overdue tasks trigger escalation after 48 hours counted from the task due date (the 24 hours before the Overdue flag are part of those 48).
attrs.rationale: Milestone and Task Rule 2. Workflow 3 C1: the Overdue flag is set at 24 hours and the task escalates at 48 hours.

nodes.title: Missed task: reminder, Overdue flag after 24 hours, team contacts patient

attrs.statement: When a patient misses a scheduled task, the system sends a reminder notification; after 24 hours the system sets the Overdue flag on the task (Overdue is a flag, not a status) and the aftercare team contacts the patient.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 alternative flow C1.

nodes.title: Progress is completed scan, questionnaire and education tasks over total such tasks, equally weighted, real time

attrs.statement: Progress = (completed scan, questionnaire and education tasks / total such tasks) * 100; a Missed task counts as not done. Tasks are weighted equally; medication adherence is not part of the percentage. Progress updates in real time.
attrs.rationale: Milestone and Task Rule 3; Screen 1 business rules add that tasks include scan uploads, questionnaires and medication adherence. Workflow 3 step 4 states progress as completed tasks over total tasks.

nodes.title: Concerning responses flag the case Urgent and trigger escalation

attrs.statement: When a patient reports concerning symptoms or a questionnaire response triggers the urgent flag per milestone rules, the system flags the case as Urgent, the aftercare team immediately contacts the patient and the escalation workflow is triggered.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 alternative flow C2; Screen 3 business rules (urgent flag raised immediately in real-time validation).

nodes.title: Patient contact 24/7 with 2-hour urgent and 24-hour standard response

attrs.statement: Patients can contact the aftercare team 24/7. Urgent cases receive priority response within 2 hours. Standard cases receive a response within 24 hours.
attrs.rationale: Communication Rule 1.

nodes.title: Provider and aftercare team communication, immediate escalation response, audit logging

attrs.statement: Providers can communicate with the aftercare team about assigned cases. Escalations require immediate response. All communications are logged for audit.
attrs.rationale: Communication Rule 2; Screen 14 (all communications monitored and logged).

nodes.title: Admin communicates with any stakeholder, announcements, emergency bypass

attrs.statement: Admin can communicate with any stakeholder. System-wide announcements are sent to all relevant parties. Emergency communications bypass normal channels.
attrs.rationale: Communication Rule 3.

nodes.title: Aftercare data retention follows the system retention rule

attrs.statement: Retention of aftercare data, scan media and communication logs follows the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period, REQ-SYS-002.
attrs.rationale: Data and Privacy Rule 1.

nodes.title: Admin access and access attempts logged for audit

attrs.statement: Admin access is logged for the audit trail. Access attempts are logged and monitored.
attrs.rationale: Data Access Rule 2 and Data Security Rule 3.

nodes.title: Admin can edit all aftercare data and override calculated progress

attrs.statement: Admin can edit ALL aftercare data in the system, modify any provider's aftercare plans, change patient assignments and providers, and override any system-calculated progress.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rule 1; Workflow 4 step 2; Screens 8, 13 and 14 (full editability, admin override).

nodes.title: Admin edit capabilities by data area

attrs.statement: Admin can edit aftercare plans (templates, milestones, medications, instructions), patient data (patient information, treatment details, contact info), provider data (assignments, customizations, settings), progress data (progress calculations, milestone completions), communication data (messages, escalations, notifications; the original text of an edited message is kept in the edit history) and template data (milestone templates, questionnaires, resources).
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rule 2.

nodes.title: Admin edits logged with reason, history kept, parties notified

attrs.statement: All admin edits are logged with timestamp and admin identification. A change reason is required for all modifications. Edit history is maintained for the audit trail. Provider and patient are notified of significant changes.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rule 3; Screen 11 business rules.

nodes.title: Rejected standalone requests refunded automatically

attrs.statement: Any payment already taken is refunded in full and automatically when a request is rejected by the admin (an add-on too, after payment) or a standalone request stays unassigned for 7 days. A request that expires unpaid after 48 hours, or that the patient cancels at a changed price, had no payment taken, so nothing is refunded. Rejection requires a reason.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 1; Payment Rule 4 (refund policy); Screens 7 and 15 business rules; Workflow 2 alternative flow B2. Money movement is executed through FR-007.

nodes.title: Payment disputes handled by admin team

attrs.statement: Payment disputes are handled by the admin team.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 1.

nodes.title: Provider compensation for aftercare participation, paid monthly

attrs.statement: Providers are compensated for aftercare participation. Compensation is based on case complexity and duration. Payment is processed monthly.
attrs.rationale: Provider Compensation, Payment Rule 2; Workflow 1 A2 (provider receives compensation when the Hairline aftercare team takes over).

nodes.title: Platform commission 15-25% of the aftercare price when a provider delivers

attrs.statement: Platform commission is deducted from standalone and post-treatment add-on aftercare payments when a provider delivers; no commission line applies when the Hairline team keeps the full price (REQ-011-057). The commission rate is 15-25% (configurable); it is a percentage of the aftercare price, one amount under one setting, taken from the aftercare price and never added to the patient's total. Commission is calculated at time of payment.
attrs.rationale: Platform Commission, Payment Rule 3; Screen 7 business rules.

nodes.title: Templates define their own pricing, per currency, in local currency

attrs.statement: Each aftercare template defines its own pricing (fixed, subscription, or both) in Screen 16. Pricing is configured per currency, and the patient sees the price in local currency based on location.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4 (template-based pricing, multi-currency); Screen 6 and Screen 16 business rules (purchasable templates require pricing for all supported currencies; real-time exchange rates are a baseline with admin override).

nodes.title: Patient chooses fixed or subscription when template offers both

attrs.statement: If a template offers both fixed and subscription pricing, the patient chooses the pricing option at purchase time; the pricing option is separate from the payment method (card or PayPal).
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4; Screens 6 and 16.

nodes.title: Subscription charged monthly, first payment immediate

attrs.statement: Subscription payments are monthly installments charged automatically for the template duration; the first payment is immediate and subsequent payments fall on the monthly anniversary. Total subscription amount = monthly price x template duration in months.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4; Screens 7 and 16.

nodes.title: Post-treatment add-on only within 90 days of Hairline treatment completion

attrs.statement: The post-treatment add-on is available only to Hairline-treated patients within 90 days of treatment completion; the system verifies a completed Hairline treatment within 90 days and auto-populates treatment information from the patient's treatment history.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4; Screen 6; Workflow 2b step 1.

nodes.title: Standalone service available to all patients

attrs.statement: The standalone service is available to all patients regardless of treatment source.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4.

nodes.title: Only templates marked Available for Purchase shown, filtered by treatment type

attrs.statement: Only templates marked "Available for Purchase" are shown, filtered by treatment type compatibility. Templates can be marked "Internal Use Only" (providers only) or "Available for Purchase" (standalone and add-on). The template name is used as the service name for patient-facing display.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4; Screens 6 and 16.

nodes.title: Price locked at purchase

attrs.statement: Patients are locked into the price at the time of purchase; future template price changes do not affect existing patients. Pricing changes to active templates require admin approval.
attrs.rationale: Payment Rule 4 (pricing immutability); Screen 16 business rules.

nodes.title: Submitted standalone request goes to Pending Assignment, admin assigns provider

attrs.statement: After the patient submits a standalone request, with no payment taken, it appears as Pending Assignment in the admin dashboard (Screen 15); the admin reviews patient information and treatment details, assigns a suitable provider based on specialization and availability, and the system notifies the assigned provider.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 steps 1-2; Screen 15 business rules.

nodes.title: Assigned provider configures the plan; payment activates a standalone plan; patient onboarded

attrs.statement: The assigned provider reviews the patient case, selects the aftercare template (the purchased one, or an alternative that offers the chosen pricing option, REQ-011-100; in the paid add-on only at the price already paid) and customizes the plan. For a standalone request the provider completes the plan, the request becomes Payment due, the plan is not active until payment succeeds and the system notifies the patient that payment is now due; for a post-treatment add-on the provider activates the plan. On activation the patient receives an activation notification and gains access to the aftercare dashboard (Screen 1) and the aftercare team begins monitoring.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 steps 3-5 and Workflow 2b steps 4-5. Standalone order: request, admin assigns, provider configures, payment activates.

nodes.title: Failed payment can retry; request expires after 48 hours unpaid

attrs.statement: When payment fails the patient receives a failure notification and can retry with a different payment method; the request becomes Expired after 48 hours without successful payment (standalone: counted from the payment-due notice; add-on: counted from the failed payment). Nothing was charged, so nothing is refunded.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 alternative B1, Workflow 2b B1b; Screen 7 business rules (failed payments allow retry). Screen 15 separately says requests expire after 7 days if not assigned.

nodes.title: Admin rejection marks request Not suitable and notifies patient with reason

attrs.statement: When the admin rejects a request, the admin marks it "Not suitable for aftercare" with a required reason and the patient receives a rejection notification with the reason.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 alternative B2; Screen 15. Refund is a separate rule.

nodes.title: No available provider: Awaiting provider availability, admin assigns manually

attrs.statement: When no suitable provider is available, the admin marks the request "Awaiting provider availability", the patient is notified of the delay and the admin manually assigns when a provider becomes available. The 7-day unassigned timer of REQ-011-053 pauses while the request carries this mark and resumes when it is cleared.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 alternative B3.

nodes.title: Unassigned standalone requests are rejected after 7 days; an add-on has no unassigned expiry

attrs.statement: A standalone request not assigned within 7 days of submission, with the time paused while the request is Awaiting provider availability, becomes Rejected with a system reason and the refund rule applies. A post-treatment add-on has no unassigned expiry because assignment is automatic at payment; its reminder and escalation follow REQ-011-090.
attrs.rationale: Screen 15 business rules.

nodes.title: Add-on assigned automatically after payment: original provider if Active and participating, otherwise the Hairline team

attrs.statement: Payment confirmation of a post-treatment add-on triggers automatic assignment: the system assigns the original treatment provider if the provider is Active and has the aftercare participation setting on (a standing yes or no setting on the provider profile, owned by FR-015), otherwise the Hairline aftercare team; the patient is notified of the provider assignment and the assigned provider receives a notification.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2b step 3 and alternative B1a.

nodes.title: Provider marks completion, configures plan from admin-created template

attrs.statement: Treatment-linked setup starts on the FR-010 completion signal. The provider selects an admin-created milestone template, adds patient-specific instructions and post-operative medications (name, dosage, frequency, special instructions), may modify milestone durations and confirms the plan; the system then generates the plan with milestones, creates the patient aftercare dashboard, sends an activation notification to the patient and sends the aftercare team a case assignment notification.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 steps 1-4; Screen 10 business rules.

nodes.title: Paperwork-only aftercare: instructions delivered, no monitoring

attrs.statement: When the provider marks "Paperwork only - no aftercare service" and uploads an aftercare instructions document, the patient receives the instructions but no active monitoring, and the patient status moves to Completed after instruction delivery. The setup row closes with no plan, the closing rule applies (REQ-011-101) and the completion event carries the outcome paperwork only; a later add-on stays allowed (REQ-011-092).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative A1.

nodes.title: Who is paid depends on who delivers; a provider who hands aftercare to the Hairline team gets a fixed handover fee

attrs.statement: When the provider marks "Assign to Hairline aftercare team", the admin receives a notification for aftercare assignment, the Hairline aftercare team takes over patient monitoring, and, after the handover, the coordinator confirms the plan on Screen 14 and the system activates it. The provider is paid a fixed handover fee set by the admin (default 0, so nothing is paid until the admin sets an amount); in the treatment-linked flow there is no separate aftercare price, so Hairline pays the fee from its own revenue, and in the add-on and standalone flows Hairline keeps the rest of the price. The fee is a Handover Fee credit entry on the clinic's balance record owned by FR-017 (REQ-017-203). When the Hairline team delivers by default in the add-on flow, or after an admin reassignment, Hairline keeps the full price with no commission line and no provider payment. When a provider delivers, the provider is paid the price less commission (REQ-011-040).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative A2.

nodes.title: System sends reminders for upcoming tasks and missed doses

attrs.statement: The system sends notifications for upcoming tasks (scan or photo set, questionnaire), scan and questionnaire reminders, and reminder notifications for missed medication doses.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 steps 1-3; Screen 4 business rules.

nodes.title: Scan upload rules

attrs.statement: The scan is validated for quality with real-time feedback and may be retaken when quality is below the threshold; maximum file size is 50MB; multiple scans within a milestone are supported per the configured scan schedule with one upload allowed per scheduled instance; the stored scan is made available to the aftercare team and previous scans remain accessible for comparison.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 step 2; Screen 2 business rules (V1 head scan photo sets; true 3D scanning is V2).

nodes.title: Questionnaire submission rules

attrs.statement: All required questionnaire fields must be completed before submission. Drafts are saved automatically every 30 seconds. The patient may retake and resubmit the questionnaire while its task is open; the latest answer counts and earlier answers are kept in the history. The aftercare team reviews responses.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules; Workflow 3 step 3. Questionnaire content is owned by FR-025.

nodes.title: Medication schedule and adherence rules

attrs.statement: Medications are prescribed by the provider during aftercare setup. Adherence = (taken doses / total doses) * 100. A dose is shown as missed if not taken within 2 hours, and Mark as Taken is enabled when the dose time is reached. History is available for the entire aftercare period.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and field validation.

nodes.title: Educational resources are milestone-specific and viewing is tracked

attrs.statement: Educational resources are specific to the current milestone, viewing progress is tracked for compliance, resources remain accessible throughout aftercare and new resources added by admin appear automatically.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules.

nodes.title: Order and checkout rules

attrs.statement: Payment is processed through FR-007 with multiple payment methods (credit or debit cards, PayPal, local payment methods) and PCI-compliant processing; terms and privacy policy must be accepted; payment confirmation activates the aftercare plan for a standalone request (Workflow 2, after the provider has configured the plan) and triggers automatic assignment for a post-treatment add-on (Workflow 2b), plus a confirmation email. Card number, expiry, CVV, cardholder name and billing address are entered in the payment form and are not stored by FR-011.
attrs.rationale: Screen 7 business rules and fields. Payment processing is owned by FR-007.

nodes.title: Provider list limited to assigned patients with overdue indicator

attrs.statement: The provider case list shows only patients assigned to this provider, with overdue cases shown with amber indicators; progress is calculated automatically by the system.
attrs.rationale: Screens 8 and 12 business rules.

nodes.title: Case details keep full history for Hairline-treated and standalone cases

attrs.statement: The provider case details screen displays all historical data from the patient's entire journey without removing older data: for Hairline-treated patients the complete lifecycle (inquiry, quote, treatment details, aftercare), for standalone patients only aftercare data and the intake information from the request. All activities are logged with timestamps, the provider can modify the plan only for assigned patients and an escalation creates an audit trail.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 business rules.

nodes.title: Setup wizard needs all steps; admin can edit after activation

attrs.statement: All setup steps must be completed before activation, the provider can go back to previous steps, the system validates all required fields, the admin can edit any step after activation and the patient receives a notification upon activation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 10 business rules.

nodes.title: Plan edits are logged; major changes need admin approval

attrs.statement: Provider changes are logged and tracked, admin changes override provider settings, major changes require admin approval (proposed with a reason and approved or rejected per REQ-011-098), all changes are logged with reason and timestamp, the patient is notified of approved changes and change history is maintained for the audit trail.
attrs.rationale: Screen 11 business rules.

nodes.title: Admin list shows all cases, overdue amber, actions logged

attrs.statement: The admin case list shows all aftercare cases across all providers, any case data is editable, overdue cases are shown with amber indicators, progress is calculated automatically and all actions are logged for the audit trail.
attrs.rationale: Screens 13 and 14 business rules.

nodes.title: Provider assignment based on specialization and availability

attrs.statement: Provider assignment is based on specialization and availability; the admin sees available providers with name, specialization and availability.
attrs.rationale: Screen 15 business rules and fields.

nodes.title: Template lifecycle: not deletable in use, approval for active changes, tested first

attrs.statement: Templates cannot be deleted if in use, changes to active templates require approval, new templates must be tested before activation and resource files are limited to 100MB each.
attrs.rationale: Screen 16 business rules.

nodes.title: Questionnaire sets selected per milestone from FR-025 Aftercare and Multi-Context sets

attrs.statement: Screen 16 selects among existing Questionnaire Sets and configures schedule and frequency per milestone; each milestone independently selects one Questionnaire Set; the sets surfaced are Aftercare sets plus every Multi-Context set. Assigning a set to a milestone and replacing it are written to the audit trail with the set version, and each response stores the set version. Sets and questions are not authored in FR-011.
attrs.rationale: Screen 16 business rules; content ownership is FR-025.

nodes.title: Provider withdrawal reviewed by admin

attrs.statement: When a provider withdraws from aftercare, the admin receives a notification and reviews the case, and can reassign it to another suitable provider, assign it to the Hairline internal aftercare team or mark the aftercare as cancelled with a reason; all changes are logged and the patient is notified of the new arrangement or cancellation.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 alternative D1. Provider performance reassignment (D2) and template and process updates (D3) are admin actions covered by the admin override and reassignment rules.

nodes.title: Treatment-linked cases are not cancelled on provider suspension or deactivation

attrs.statement: For treatment-linked cases the aftercare case is not cancelled and the booking stays Aftercare when the assigned provider is suspended or deactivated; the cause and the supportRequired marker are recorded and an admin reassigns the aftercare provider or team on Screen 19.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 D4 and D5, General Module Rule 4. The standalone behaviour is REQ-011-014.

nodes.title: Suspension and withdrawal handling keeps records read-only and removes provider actions

attrs.statement: On provider suspension, deactivation or reassignment the provider loses aftercare actions on the case; the completion milestone, plan, milestones, scans, questionnaire responses, medications and communication history are retained read-only; the cancellation is not a patient cancellation or a provider withdrawal; a later deactivation does not overwrite an earlier ProviderSuspended cause; no refund occurs automatically.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 D4 and D5; General Module Rule 4.

nodes.title: Reassignment keeps the case and the previous provider read-only history

attrs.statement: A reassignment changes only the aftercare provider or team; the plan, milestones, scans, questionnaire responses, medications and communication history stay with the case, the new assignee gets the aftercare actions from the moment of confirmation, the previous provider loses them and keeps read-only access to history it recorded, and a reassignment has no automatic refund and no refund ladder: for a standalone plan any refund is an admin manual refund (REQ-007-100); for a treatment-linked case reached through the FR-006 B7 decision, the refund and payout hold are those set on FR-006 Screen 11 (REQ-006-019). The setup clock of REQ-011-090 restarts at the admin assignment and addresses the new assignee, and Screen 19 marks a provider handover differently from an admin reassignment.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 D5 and Screen 19 business rules.

nodes.title: Reassignment saved only after confirmation, with audit and optional marker resolution

attrs.statement: The reassignment is saved only after confirmation, is recorded in the audit trail with admin identity, timestamp, reason, previous assignee and new assignee and, when selected, records the audited resolution of the supportRequired marker; the new provider must be an Active provider other than the current one; the reason is 10 to 1000 characters.
attrs.rationale: Screen 19 fields and business rules.

nodes.title: Provider performance scores monthly (backlog)

attrs.statement: Provider performance scores are calculated monthly, poor performance triggers a review process and provider suspension requires admin approval. Retention of performance data follows the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period, REQ-SYS-002.
attrs.rationale: Screen 17 business rules. The screen is Backlog (post-MVP analytics).

nodes.title: Admin progress overview updates in real time, metrics daily (backlog)

attrs.statement: The admin progress overview shows all cases across all providers with real-time updates, performance metrics calculated daily, alerts generated automatically for issues and all actions logged with admin identification.
attrs.rationale: Screen 18 business rules. The screen is Backlog (post-MVP analytics).

nodes.title: Scan media is V1 photo sets

attrs.statement: In V1 all references to 3D scans in this FR refer to standardized head scan photo sets (multiple 2D views); true 3D scanning (ARKit/ARCore) is deferred to V2.
attrs.rationale: Executive Summary note on scan media.

nodes.title: Out of scope: patient and provider chat, payment flows beyond activation

attrs.statement: Direct patient to provider chat is out of scope (handled by FR-012; that conversation stays open while the pair has live aftercare and becomes read-only once nothing live is left between them (FR-012 REQ-012-018)) and payment flows beyond standalone activation are out of scope (Payment FR).
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure, Out of Scope.

nodes.title: Network loss during scan upload

attrs.statement: Network loss during scan upload: resumable upload; no duplicate entries
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Edge Cases (PRD line 1677).

nodes.title: Conflicting schedule changes

attrs.statement: Conflicting schedule changes: latest confirmed change supersedes prior; audit preserved
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Edge Cases (PRD line 1678).

nodes.title: Refund policy

attrs.statement: Full refund if request rejected by admin; prorated refund for subscription cancellations based on unused months (REQ-011-097 states the outcome per payment plan)
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Payment Rule 4 (PRD line 1435).

nodes.title: Multi-currency pricing baseline and override

attrs.statement: Multi-currency pricing uses real-time exchange rates as baseline but allows admin override for final pricing
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Screen 16 Business Rules (PRD line 1140).

nodes.title: Purchasable template pricing

attrs.statement: Purchasable templates require pricing configuration for all supported currencies
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Screen 16 Business Rules (PRD line 1136).

nodes.title: Overdue task highlight

attrs.statement: Overdue tasks highlighted in red
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Screen 1 Business Rules (PRD line 397).

nodes.title: Completed task highlight

attrs.statement: Completed tasks shown in green
attrs.rationale: Verbatim from the frozen PRD: Screen 1 Business Rules (PRD line 395).

nodes.title: Default patient progress reminder, monthly for 12 months

attrs.statement: By default System MUST send each patient a progress reminder once a month for 12 months after treatment; the patient MAY change or switch off the reminder, and the default is admin-editable. The reminders stop when the plan completes (REQ-011-096).
attrs.rationale: Communication Rule 4 (Default Patient Progress Reminder).

nodes.title: Medication picked only from the admin-managed medication list

attrs.statement: The provider MUST pick each aftercare medication only from the Active templates of the admin-managed medication list (the FR-024 medication templates); free-text medication names are not allowed. The plan keeps its own copy of the text, so a later template edit or deactivation does not change it.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 483, 785 (Medication Name: must be a medication template owned by FR-024; no free-text medication names).

nodes.title: Plan not finished: assignee reminder after 2 days, admin escalation after 4 days

attrs.statement: When an aftercare plan is not finished, System MUST remind the assignee after 2 days and escalate the case to the admin after 4 days; both day counts are admin settings. The days count from the FR-010 completion signal (treatment-linked), from payment for a paid add-on whose plan is not activated, and from assignment for a standalone request whose provider has not finished the plan; the clock restarts at a handover or an admin assignment and addresses the current assignee. The admin can reassign on Screen 19 or, for a treatment-linked plan or a paid add-on, activate the plan manually (REQ-011-019).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 Alternative Flow A3; General Module Rule 1.

nodes.title: FR-010 completion signal opens setup; early close opens it for the assigned team; a repeated signal returns the existing plan

attrs.statement: Aftercare setup (Workflow 1) opens on the FR-010 treatment completion signal; FR-006 owns the move of the booking to Aftercare. When FR-010 closes treatment early, setup opens for the aftercare team or the reassigned provider after the admin assigns them on Screen 19. A repeated completion signal for the same booking MUST return the existing plan and create no second plan. The retry of a failed signal stays in FR-010 (REQ-010-086).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 Trigger, A4 and A5; FR-010 and FR-006 integration points.

nodes.title: No add-on while a plan for the same booking is Pending activation, Active or Completed

attrs.statement: System MUST refuse a post-treatment add-on while a plan for the same booking is Pending activation, Active or Completed, and allow it after a paperwork-only completion. A plan is Pending activation from the opening of setup at the FR-010 completion signal (treatment-linked) or from configuration until payment (standalone); a paperwork-only completion closes the opened setup row with no plan.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2b step 1; Screen 6 business rules.

nodes.title: A standalone request may be converted from FR-038 monitoring, with an idempotency key

attrs.statement: System MUST accept a standalone request converted from an FR-038 transplant-progress monitoring case, carrying the source, the monitoring case, the scan or photo set, the report file and an idempotency key; a repeated key returns the existing request, and a new standalone request after a Rejected or Expired converted request uses a new idempotency key. The patient still picks the template and pricing option.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points; Workflow 2 step 1; Screen 6 business rules. Agreed with the FR-038 hand-off.

nodes.title: A conversion is refused after the monitoring case is completed; a failed or abandoned request returns the patient to FR-038 Screen 6

attrs.statement: System MUST refuse a conversion once the monitoring case is completed, and after a failed or abandoned request MUST return the patient to FR-038 Screen 6 with the draft intact (REQ-038-068). When a converted request ends Rejected or Expired, the notice says the patient may start a new standalone request pre-filled from the same source data; the monitoring case stays final.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 step 1; Screen 6 business rules.

nodes.title: Scan task uses the FR-002 media-only call with the scan id as idempotency key

attrs.statement: The scan task MUST use the FR-002 media-only call (REQ-002-047) with at least one photo and the scan id as idempotency key, so a retried upload never creates a second scan; staged photos that are never attached to a scan are removed after 7 days (REQ-002-051).
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules; FR-002 integration point.

nodes.title: Plan completes at the end of the last milestone or the subscription term

attrs.statement: System MUST complete the plan at the end of the last milestone or the end of the subscription term, whichever is later, stop all reminders for the plan (including the progress reminder of REQ-011-088) and emit a completion event that FR-006 reads (REQ-006-060); every other ending follows REQ-011-101.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 Alternative Flow C3.

nodes.title: Patient can cancel an aftercare subscription or a plan paid in full

attrs.statement: The patient MUST be able to cancel from the plan payment screen (Screen 7). A monthly subscription runs to the end of the paid month, later months are not charged, the plan then becomes Cancelled, and nothing is refunded. A plan paid in full stops at the end of the current month and the unused full months are refunded pro rata (REQ-011-083). Commission and provider payout follow the refund in the same proportion. The commission reversal is FR-017 REQ-017-202.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 Alternative Flow C4; Payment Rule 4 (refund policy). Money movement is executed through FR-007 and FR-017.

nodes.title: Extensions and major changes are proposed by the provider or coordinator and decided by the admin

attrs.statement: The assigned provider (or the Aftercare Coordinator when the Hairline team delivers) MUST be able to propose an extension or major change with a reason. The admin approves or rejects it on the admin case screen (approval status Proposed, Approved or Rejected) and the patient is notified. Where the change costs more, the patient MUST accept and pay before it takes effect. A rejection leaves the plan unchanged and the proposer is told why. When the coordinator proposes, the approving admin MUST be a different person.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 Alternative Flow D6; Screens 11 and 14 business rules.

nodes.title: Urgent flag with raised-at time, cleared with a note, escalated to the admin after 2 hours

attrs.statement: The plan MUST carry an urgent flag and the time it was raised, set by an urgent questionnaire answer or a manual flag. The assigned provider (or the coordinator when the Hairline team delivers) clears it with a note. When the flag is not cleared within 2 hours of the raised time (clearing it with a note is the response), System MUST escalate the case to the admin. Dashboards count the plans that have the flag set.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 3 Alternative Flow C2; Communication Rule 1; Screens 9, 12, 13 and 14.

nodes.title: Alternative template only among those offering the chosen pricing option; in the paid add-on only at the price already paid; the patient accepts a changed standalone price or cancels at no charge

attrs.statement: The provider MAY pick an alternative template only among templates that offer the pricing option the patient chose. Screen 7 shows the order summary of the final template; when the final price differs from the requested price the patient MUST accept the new price before paying, or may cancel at no charge, in which case the request becomes Rejected with the system reason cancelled by patient. In the post-treatment add-on flow, which is already paid, an alternative is allowed only if its price for the chosen pricing option equals the price already paid (REQ-011-047).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 step 3 and Alternative Flow B4; Workflow 2b step 4; Screen 7 business rules.

nodes.title: Every ending of aftercare stops all reminders and emits the completion event with an outcome; an admin can cancel with a reason

attrs.statement: Every ending of aftercare (completed, paperwork-only completion, cancelled by the patient through subscription cancellation once the paid period ends, cancelled by an admin) MUST stop all reminders for the plan and emit the completion event with an outcome value; the booking then moves to Completed as it does on a normal completion, which FR-006 reads. The admin MUST be able to cancel aftercare on Screen 14 Tab 4 with a mandatory reason, and the cancellation is written to the audit trail.

nodes.title: Contact Support sends a message to the aftercare team

attrs.statement: Contact Support on the patient Aftercare Dashboard (Screen 1) MUST let the patient send a text message to the aftercare team at any time while the aftercare plan is open. System MUST record it as an aftercare communication entry (entry type message, sender role patient) on the plan and show it in the aftercare team's communication log for that patient. It is not an FR-012 conversation, and FR-012 chat with the provider stays separate (REQ-011-080).

nodes.title: Aftercare team messages reach the patient in the app with a notification

attrs.statement: When a member of the aftercare team sends the patient a message from the aftercare case, including a reply to a Contact Support message, System MUST record it as an aftercare communication entry (entry type message, sender role aftercare_team), MUST show it to the patient in the Messages list on the Aftercare Dashboard (Screen 1) together with the patient's own Contact Support messages in chronological order, and MUST send the patient the `aftercare.team_message` notification by push and email (FR-030 REQ-030-295). The patient answers through Contact Support (REQ-011-102).
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, owner ruling 2026-11-25.

nodes.title: One conversation per patient-provider pair, created at the first quote

attrs.statement: System MUST automatically create a new conversation between patient and provider when provider submits their first quote for patient inquiry; subsequent quotes from same provider to same patient MUST add inquiry/quote IDs to existing conversation (one conversation per patient-provider pair). The provider side of the pair is the clinic: every clinic team member with messaging permission reads and replies in the same conversation. The unread count is kept once per clinic: when one team member opens the conversation it counts as read for the whole clinic.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 938.

nodes.title: Patient Messages Inbox sortable by latest activity, provider name or date created

attrs.statement: System MUST provide a Messages Inbox view for patients showing all conversations, sortable by latest activity, provider name, or date created. Search and filtering of the inbox is stated once in REQ-022-070 (first release).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Search and filtering moved to REQ-022-070.

nodes.title: Provider Messages popup in header navigation

attrs.statement: System MUST provide a Messages popup/submenu in header navigation for providers showing recent conversations (max 10) with unread counts and quick access to patient chats.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 940.

nodes.title: Admin Communication Monitoring Center lists all conversations

attrs.statement: System MUST provide a Communication Monitoring Center for admins as the message list of all conversations. Its filters, how they combine, and that they are remembered are stated once in REQ-022-122.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Filters moved to REQ-022-122.

nodes.title: Admin Message Thread View with monitoring and emergency states

attrs.statement: System MUST provide a detailed Message Thread View for admins with two states: Screen 6A (default monitoring/flagging state with read-only access) and Screen 6B (activated emergency intervention state with message composition), accessible when conversation is selected from monitoring center.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 942.

nodes.title: In-app Patient to Provider messaging only through the Messages screens

attrs.statement: System MUST enable in-app messaging for Patient ↔ Provider with text and media, accessible ONLY through dedicated Messages/Inbox screens (chat is not embedded in quote detail screens; a quote screen may link to the conversation in the inbox, REQ-005-015).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 943.

nodes.title: Real-time message notifications and unread badge updates

attrs.statement: System MUST deliver real-time notifications for new messages to intended recipients (patients, providers, and both parties when admin intervenes); update unread badges in inbox views and header popup menus. The notification events are defined in the FR-030 event catalogue. The intervention notice to both parties and the admin keyword alert cannot be switched off or held; the other chat notices follow the user's notification settings.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. The events are catalogued in FR-030 (REQ-030-061).

nodes.title: Complete conversation history with timestamps and read receipts

attrs.statement: Users MUST be able to view complete conversation history with timestamps and read receipts.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 945.

nodes.title: Attachment type and size limits with specific feedback

attrs.statement: System MUST enforce attachment type and size limits (Images: JPG/PNG max 5MB; Video: MP4 max 10MB; PDF: max 10MB; max 5 attachments per message) and provide specific user feedback on violations. The checks and the malware scan run on every attachment from a patient, provider or admin; a file that fails is refused with a specific message and the message can still be sent without it.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 946.

nodes.title: Message lifecycle events, flags, emergency interventions, calls and moderation setting changes logged for audit

attrs.statement: System MUST log message lifecycle events (sent, delivered, read) and these audit events: attachment sent, keyword flag raised, manual flag raised, system flag raised, flag status changed, emergency intervention enabled, the emergency intervention message, call entry, and moderation setting changed.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 942.

nodes.title: Admins flag conversations manually with flag type and optional notes

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to manually flag conversations for observation with flag type selection (Off-Platform Risk / Potential Dispute / Quality Concern / Follow-Up Needed / Other) and optional internal notes.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 948.

nodes.title: Automatic keyword flags red, manual flags orange; flagging notifies nobody

attrs.statement: System MUST distinguish between automatic keyword flags (red) and manual observation flags (orange) in admin monitoring center and thread detail view; flagging must NOT notify patient or provider. Exception for the provider's view: the provider's conversation screen still shows the flag indicator for an open flag of any type (the patient is still not notified).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. The provider sees the flag indicator on Screen 4.

nodes.title: Admin sends messages only for emergencies with a mandatory reason

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to send messages in patient-provider conversations ONLY for emergency situations with mandatory reason tracking (Policy Violation / Urgent Dispute / Patient Safety).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md Screen 6B. The reason options are Policy Violation, Urgent Dispute and Patient Safety.

nodes.title: Admin messages carry the Hairline Admin badge for both parties

attrs.statement: System MUST clearly identify admin messages with "Hairline Admin" badge visible to both patient and provider.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 951.

nodes.title: Conversation metadata kept per patient-provider pair and searchable

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain conversations per patient-provider pair with searchable metadata (patient ID, provider ID, inquiry ID, quote reference, status, unread_count, keyword flags, manual observation flags, admin_intervened flag, emergency_reason, last_message_at).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 957.

nodes.title: Flag history stored per conversation

attrs.statement: System MUST store flag history for each conversation including flag type, timestamp, admin user, status (active / resolved / escalated_to_intervention / intervention_completed; "Resolved - No Action Needed" shows as resolved), and internal notes.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary.

nodes.title: Attachments stored securely with access controls and metadata

attrs.statement: System MUST store attachments securely with links to their parent messages, access controls, and metadata (file type, size, upload timestamp, thumbnail URLs for images/videos).
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 959.

nodes.title: Messaging enabled only after the provider sent a quote; conversation read-only when nothing live is left

attrs.statement: System MUST enable patient-provider messaging only when provider has sent a quote to patient. The conversation is open while the pair has a live quote, booking or aftercare; it becomes read-only (history kept for both parties, nobody can send, admins can still view it) when the provider is deactivated, when the provider is suspended and the pair has no open In Progress or Aftercare case (a suspended provider may still chat on those, FR-015 REQ-015-077), when the patient's account is suspended or deleted, or when nothing live is left between the pair. It opens again when the patient's suspension is lifted or ends (FR-016 REQ-016-224) and when the same provider sends a new quote. Read-only is derived from those conditions and is not a stored conversation status. On a read-only conversation the composer, attach control and call buttons are disabled with a banner giving the reason, and Enable Emergency Intervention is not available.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 963.

nodes.title: Message and media encryption follows the system PRD

attrs.statement: Encryption of message content and media in transit and at rest follows the encryption record in the system PRD.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. Encryption is stated once in REQ-SYS-004; the role-based access part is retired into REQ-SYS-009.

nodes.title: Messages and attachments retained for the system retention period

attrs.statement: System MUST retain messages and attachments as set by the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary. The retention period is stated once in REQ-SYS-002. Admin conversation export is deferred; see REQ-012-076.

nodes.title: Admin monitoring access to all conversations; intervention emergency-only

attrs.statement: Admin MUST have monitoring access to all patient-provider conversations with manual flagging capability and EMERGENCY-ONLY intervention capability.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 966.

nodes.title: All admin actions logged for compliance audit

attrs.statement: System MUST log all admin actions (manual flags, flag status changes, enabling emergency intervention, emergency interventions, moderation setting changes) with timestamp, admin user, reason/notes, and action type for compliance audit.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary, prd.md line 968.

nodes.title: Intervention restricted to authorized admin roles; intervention rate shown against a 5 percent monitoring target
