nodes.title: Every delete is a soft delete except the passport number and passport photo; protected categories restricted; cancelled inquiries and cascade records retained

attrs.statement: Every delete MUST be a soft delete (REQ-SYS-003): the record is archived or anonymised in place and is never physically removed before the retention period ends (REQ-SYS-002). The one named exception is the passport number and passport photo, which are physically erased at an approved deletion (FR-008 REQ-008-069); all other travel data is anonymised in place. The protected categories (Medical Records, Financial Records, Account Profile) are additionally restricted, with access limited to the legal purpose. Patient-cancelled inquiries (FR-003 Workflow 5), inquiries cancelled by the system when a deletion request is approved (REQ-023-042), and all records generated from the cancellation cascade — including auto-cancelled quotes with status "Cancelled (Inquiry Cancelled)" per FR-004 — are subject to the same retention rules as completed inquiries and quotes. AcceptanceEvents are retained and never deleted (FR-005 REQ-005-023). This applies to inquiry records, quote records, acceptance events (including superseded AcceptanceEvents per FR-005), and associated audit trail entries, which are kept unchanged (REQ-023-011).
attrs.rationale: Owner default 67: every category is anonymised or archived in place (REQ-SYS-002, REQ-SYS-003). Owner default 73 narrows it: the passport number and passport photo are erased at an approved deletion, as FR-008 REQ-008-069 says. Cancelled records produced at approval fall under the same retention.

nodes.title: Deletion request: no category physically removed except the passport number and passport photo; non-protected data anonymised or archived in place, protected records retained anonymised with restricted access

attrs.statement: System MUST allow patients to request data deletion (erasure). On an approved request no category is physically removed, except the passport number and passport photo named in REQ-023-003 (REQ-SYS-002, REQ-SYS-003): the personal data of the non-protected categories (Communications, Media, Analytics) is anonymised in place, or archived and made inaccessible; the protected categories (Medical Records, Financial Records, Account Profile) are retained in anonymised form, with strict access restrictions and documented legal basis.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 67: anonymise or archive in place for every category; protected categories are Medical Records, Financial Records and Account Profile.

nodes.title: Patient data anonymized in analytics and reports

attrs.statement: System MUST anonymize patient data in analytics and reports (no direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers masked or aggregated).
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Executive Summary (anonymizes patient data used in analytics) and Success Criteria (0% personally identifiable patient attributes in analytics dashboards or reports).

nodes.title: Audit log of all read and write access to protected records

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain audit logs for all read and write access to protected records, including actor, timestamp, object, action, outcome. The medical data access log and admin action log (FR-016) and the patient audit log (FR-001) feed this one audit record.
attrs.rationale: The FR-016 access and action logs and the FR-001 patient audit log feed the one audit record (ENT-audit-log-entry).

nodes.title: Admin views for retention configuration and DSR queues

attrs.statement: System MUST provide Admin views to configure retention by data category and jurisdiction (never below 10 years, REQ-023-045) and to manage DSR queues.
attrs.rationale: Admin retention settings never go below the 10-year floor of REQ-023-045. The Admin retention screens are not specified in any FR yet, so the rule is platform-wide.

nodes.title: Patients and Admins notified of DSR status updates and outcomes

attrs.statement: System MUST notify Patients and Admins about DSR status updates and completion outcomes.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 137 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Data classified into six categories; scan media are Medical Records

attrs.statement: System MUST classify data into categories: Medical Records, Financial Records, Communications, Media, Account Profile, Analytics. Head and monitoring scan media belong to Medical Records, and every record type belongs to exactly one category (REQ-023-044).
attrs.rationale: Scan media move from Media to Medical Records so the 10-year rule covers them (owner defaults 67 and 70).

nodes.title: Each category has a retention policy and legal basis, with jurisdiction overrides

attrs.statement: Each category MUST have an assigned retention policy and legal basis (with jurisdiction overrides that may only extend the period, REQ-023-045).
attrs.rationale: Jurisdiction overrides may only extend the period (REQ-023-045).

nodes.title: Audit log entries immutable; retention follows the 10-year system rule

attrs.statement: Audit log entries MUST be immutable; their retention follows the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period. An entry is never edited and never marked deleted: after a fulfilled deletion request it is anonymised by removing the identifying data from the patient record the entry points to, so the entry stays unchanged and no longer identifies the patient.
attrs.rationale: An immutable entry cannot also be rewritten or soft-deleted, so anonymisation works on the patient record the entry points to, not on the entry.

nodes.title: Backups every 6 hours, 30-day retention, deleted personal data excluded beyond window

attrs.statement: Backups MUST occur at least every 6 hours with 30-day retention (per system PRD) and exclude already-deleted personal data beyond backup windows.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Assumptions (backups every 6 hours with 30-day retention per system PRD; deleted data may persist in backups until window expiry).

nodes.title: Deletion purges search indexes and caches

attrs.statement: Deletion actions MUST purge search indexes and caches for impacted personal data.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 148 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Anonymization removes direct identifiers and reduces re-identification risk

attrs.statement: Anonymization MUST remove direct identifiers and reduce re-identification risk for quasi-identifiers.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 149 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Analytics consent captured and opt-outs honored

attrs.statement: System MUST capture consent for analytics usage where applicable and honor opt-outs in non-essential analytics.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 150 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Admin export of audit logs and retention reports in portable formats

attrs.statement: Provide Admin export of audit logs and retention reports in portable, non-proprietary formats.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Communication Structure (compliance reporting exports downloadable by Admin) and Clarification CL-3 (audit logs included in compliance reporting, summaries unless otherwise requested).

nodes.title: Programmatic DSR submission and status for the Patient app

attrs.statement: Provide programmatic access for DSR submission/status for Patient app integration.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 155 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: DSR lifecycle events notified to internal communication channels

attrs.statement: Provide event notifications for DSR lifecycle events to internal communication channels.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 156 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Entry points to deletion, data policy, audit logs and retention settings

attrs.statement: Entry points: Patient: Profile > Delete Account. Provider: Settings → Data Policy (read-only); Activity Logs. Admin: Compliance dashboard → Retention Settings; DSR Queue; Audit Logs; Reports.
attrs.rationale: The PRD gives no Screen Specifications. The patient entry is the Delete Account screen SCR-001-16 (FR-001) and the admin DSR queue is SCR-016-08 (FR-016); the provider and admin compliance screens have no node yet.

nodes.title: Patients can view the retention policy, request deletion and receive status updates

attrs.statement: Patients can view the retention policy, request account/data deletion, and receive status updates and outcomes.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 30 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Providers can view the applicable retention and privacy policy

attrs.statement: Providers can view the applicable retention/privacy policy.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 31 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Providers cannot permanently delete protected records

attrs.statement: Providers cannot permanently delete protected records.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 31 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Providers have a read-only audit trail of their users' activity

attrs.statement: Providers have read-only access to the audit trail of activity by their users.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 31 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Admins can review audit trails of access and modifications to protected records

attrs.statement: Admins can review audit trails of access to and modifications of protected records, to investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Admin Platform scope (review audit trails) and User Story 2 (a complete audit trail so an Admin can investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance).

nodes.title: Retention enforced by scheduled jobs from the retention policy

attrs.statement: Retention is enforced by cross-cutting scheduled jobs that apply the Retention Policy of each data category to records.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Shared Services scope (cross-cutting job scheduling for retention enforcement) and Key Entities (Retention Policy is applied to records via category mapping and referenced by enforcement jobs).

nodes.title: Module boundary: no chat or video, no payment flow changes, no DPO tooling

attrs.statement: Out of scope for this module: real-time chat/video features (managed by other modules), payment flow changes beyond record retention, third-party DPO/legal tooling integrations (future consideration), and patient data export (data portability), which is not offered at launch.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 45.

nodes.title: Patient notified at each DSR status change, including blocked by obligation and denied

attrs.statement: Patients are notified of each DSR status change: submission, verification required, in progress, blocked by obligation (with the expected timeline), denied (with the reason), and fulfilled.
attrs.rationale: Adds the blocked and denied notices; the timeline message of REQ-023-038 and the reason of REQ-023-043 travel with them.

nodes.title: Admins notified of new DSRs, of an approaching deadline 7 calendar days before it, and when an obligation block ends

attrs.statement: Admins are notified of new DSRs, of an approaching deadline 7 calendar days before it on a request that is still open, and, when an obligation block ends, that the request can be approved (FR-016 REQ-016-067).
attrs.rationale: A fixed threshold of 7 calendar days (a default; no setting is added).

nodes.title: Deletion request submitted from Profile > Delete Account and verified

attrs.statement: A patient submits a deletion request from Profile > Delete Account and completes verification.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Main Flow trigger (patient requests deletion from Profile > Delete Account) and Assumptions (patients are willing and able to complete identity verification for DSRs by standard methods).

nodes.title: System classifies the patient's data by category, retention and jurisdiction

attrs.statement: System classifies the patient's data by category and applicable retention/jurisdiction when a deletion request is processed, and refreshes the classification when the Admin approves. A refresh that differs from the classification the Admin reviewed (a new jurisdiction conflict or a changed retention period) returns the request to Admin review (REQ-023-039).
attrs.rationale: Classification is refreshed at approval so it cannot be stale.

nodes.title: Admin reviews the classification and approves, denies or finds the identity proof insufficient

attrs.statement: Admin reviews the classification and approves the action before anonymization or restriction is performed; the Admin may instead deny the request (REQ-023-043) or find the identity proof insufficient (REQ-023-034).
attrs.rationale: Approval is the only path to anonymisation; deny and verification are the other two exits.

nodes.title: Deletion actions audit-logged; outcome notice lists actions and legal basis

attrs.statement: System records the anonymisation actions in the audit log and notifies the patient of the outcome once, listing the actions taken and the legal basis and scope of the retained categories. The notice goes to the contact address the system captured when the request was approved, before any anonymisation; that copy is kept only until the notice is delivered, or until its last retry has failed, and is then anonymised with the rest. The notice goes by email only (the critical dsr.fulfilled notice of the FR-020 catalogue) and creates no in-app record; when the email still fails after the last retry, the Admin sees the failure in the delivery log (FR-020 REQ-020-161).
attrs.rationale: The outcome notice is sent once, at the end of the main flow; the old second notice step is removed.

nodes.title: Admin decides whether identity proof is sufficient; Verification Required stays open until validated or denied

attrs.statement: An Admin decides at review whether the identity proof of a deletion request is sufficient. When it is not, the request is set to Verification Required and the patient is notified; the patient provides additional verification and an Admin validates it, which returns the request to Pending Admin Review. A request in Verification Required stays open until an Admin validates the proof or denies the request with a reason (REQ-023-043); it never closes by itself.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 69: no auto-close; the Admin decides insufficient proof at review and ends a stuck request with a Deny and a reason.

nodes.title: Every approval includes the Admin's confirmation that the protected categories are retained anonymised

attrs.statement: Every approval includes the Admin's confirmation that the protected categories (Medical Records, Financial Records, Account Profile) are retained in anonymised form with restricted access, because every patient account has an Account Profile; anonymisation of the other categories completes with it.
attrs.rationale: One protected list (Medical Records, Financial Records, Account Profile). Every account has an Account Profile, so the confirmation is part of every approval and the old alternative flow is merged into the main flow.

nodes.title: Concurrent DSRs merged into one request; SLA per consolidated request

attrs.statement: When a patient submits multiple DSRs concurrently, the system merges them into one request with a clear status; the SLA applies per consolidated request and the merged request keeps the earliest submission date.
attrs.rationale: A merged request keeps the earliest submission date so the clock rule has one input.

nodes.title: One list of active obligations; an obligation at approval blocks approval and the request stays pending

attrs.statement: System MUST keep one list of active obligations: an inquiry at the Accepted stage or later that is not Completed or Cancelled (FR-003 REQ-003-103), an active booking, treatment or aftercare in progress, a payment in progress, and a pending refund. At submission FR-001 blocks treatment or aftercare in progress and a payment in progress (REQ-001-091, REQ-001-092), and FR-003 states the submission block for an inquiry at the Accepted stage or later (REQ-003-103). The full list is checked at approval: the system checks it when the Admin approves, and any item blocks approval, keeps the request Pending Admin Review, marks it blocked by obligation and tells the patient the expected timeline. The expected timeline is the end date of the obligation when the owning FR knows it, otherwise the text "after the obligation completes"; no field is added. The system clears the mark when the obligation ends or an approval check passes. Nothing else is restricted for the patient while the request is pending.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 68: one list; an obligation at approval blocks approval and the request stays pending. A Completed inquiry is not an obligation (controller decision), so a patient who finished a treatment can be deleted. At submission FR-001 blocks only the items it names; the full list is checked at approval.

nodes.title: Jurisdiction conflict applies the longer retention and flags Admin review before approval

attrs.statement: On a jurisdiction conflict (for example EU versus non-EU residency), the system applies the longer retention period (REQ-023-045) and flags the request for Admin review before approval. The classification (Main Flow step 2) and the refresh at approval (step 5) set the flag; the Admin clears it by approving after reviewing the conflict. The refresh sets it only when the conflict or the retention period differs from what the Admin reviewed, and the request then returns to Pending Admin Review.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 71: stricter means longer. The review flag is a field of the request.

nodes.title: Deletion after inquiry cancellation proceeds; cancelled records stay retained; records cancelled at approval are covered

attrs.statement: A deletion request made after the patient cancelled an inquiry proceeds normally, because a cancelled inquiry is a terminal state with no active obligation. Inquiries cancelled by the patient, inquiries cancelled by the system at approval (REQ-023-042), cascaded cancelled quotes, and associated audit entries are retained per the system PRD, Platform-Wide Rules: One 10-year retention period and REQ-023-003 even after the deletion request is fulfilled; the retained inquiry and quote records are kept in anonymised form and the audit entries are kept unchanged (REQ-023-011).
attrs.rationale: Extended to inquiries cancelled by the system at approval; audit entries stay unchanged (REQ-023-011).

nodes.title: Deletion request deadline runs from submission and does not pause during verification

attrs.statement: The 30-day deadline of a deletion request always runs from submission (the earliest submission date of a merged request) and does not pause during verification or while an obligation blocks approval. A request is open in any status before Fulfilled or Denied. When the deadline passes on an open request (Pending Admin Review, Verification Required or In Progress), the queue shows it as overdue and the request stays open; an overdue request blocked by an obligation is shown as an excused breach.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 68: one clock rule. The deadline runs from submission (the earliest date of a merged request), never pauses, and an overdue open request is shown, not closed; a breach while blocked by an obligation is excused.

nodes.title: Approval cancels the patient's open inquiry through FR-003 before anything is anonymised

attrs.statement: When an Admin approves a deletion request, the system MUST cancel the patient's open inquiry through FR-003 (REQ-003-103) before any data is anonymised, so the cancellation and its provider notices run on the identifiable record. The cancellation happens at approval, never at submission; a denied request and a request blocked by an obligation cancel nothing. The cancelled inquiry and quotes are retained under REQ-023-003 and REQ-023-040. Anonymisation starts only after the FR-003 cancellation and its provider notices complete (a notice is complete when its first attempt has been handed to a channel or it has ended failed after the last retry, FR-020 REQ-020-040). If the cancellation fails, the request stays In Progress, the queue shows that it needs attention and the system retries; nothing is anonymised until the cancellation succeeds.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 63: cancel at admin approval, not at submission; a refused or blocked request cancels nothing. The cancellation runs first because it notifies providers and flips quotes on the identifiable record. FR-003 owns the cancellation (REQ-003-103).

nodes.title: Admin may deny a deletion request with a required reason; the patient is notified and nothing is cancelled or anonymised

attrs.statement: An Admin MAY deny a deletion request on the DSR Queue (FR-016) while it is Pending Admin Review (including one blocked by an obligation) or Verification Required (for example when the proof cannot be completed). Deny is not available once the request is In Progress, because the inquiry is already cancelled. A denial requires a reason; the system sets the status to Denied, notifies the patient with the reason, cancels nothing and anonymises nothing, and the request stays auditable. The patient may submit a new deletion request after a denial.
attrs.rationale: Gives the FR-016 Deny action (REQ-016-173) a counterpart in the entity FR-023 owns; a refused request cancels nothing (owner default 63). Resubmission after a denial is allowed, as a default.

nodes.title: Every record type belongs to exactly one category by the record-type mapping

attrs.statement: System MUST assign every record type to exactly one data category by the record-type mapping below. Reviews, messages and support cases are Communications and are anonymised in place. Inquiries are Medical Records, and quotes, acceptance events and bookings are Financial Records; they are retained records under REQ-023-003 and REQ-023-040. Scan media are Medical Records. Message attachments belong to their message and are anonymised in place with it. Legal acceptance records (acceptances, legal audit entries and reminders) are Account Profile.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 70: reviews, messages and support cases are Communications (anonymised); inquiry is Medical Records; quote, acceptance event and booking are Financial Records; scans are Medical Records. The mapping table lives in the PRD.

nodes.title: Retention defaults to 10 years, never below 10; a jurisdiction override may only extend

attrs.statement: The retention period of every category MUST default to 10 years and MUST NOT be set below 10 years (REQ-SYS-002). A jurisdiction override may only extend the period, and the stricter retention on a jurisdiction conflict is the longer period.
attrs.rationale: Owner default 71: the Admin retention screen cannot shorten any category below REQ-SYS-002, and the stricter retention on a conflict is the longer one.

nodes.title: Status of a deletion request is set only by the named steps; the system sets Fulfilled and FR-016 owns the certificate

attrs.statement: The status of a deletion request is set only as follows: Pending Admin Review at submission and when an Admin validates the verification; Verification Required when an Admin finds the proof insufficient; In Progress when an Admin approves and the obligation check passes; Fulfilled when the system sends the outcome notice after anonymisation; Denied when an Admin denies. The request also carries two flags: blocked by obligation (set when an obligation blocks approval, cleared by the system when the obligation ends or an approval check passes; the status stays Pending Admin Review) and jurisdiction review required (REQ-023-039). FR-016 shows the status and owns the deletion certificate (REQ-016-062); it does not set Fulfilled.
attrs.rationale: Closes the lifecycle gaps: every status has a step that sets it. Fulfilment is set by the system at the outcome notice (a default); FR-016 shows it and generates the certificate (REQ-016-062).

nodes.title: A patient can log in while a deletion request is open; at Fulfilled every session ends and the email address is free

attrs.statement: While a deletion request is open (any status before Fulfilled or Denied) the patient can still log in (FR-001 REQ-001-068). When the request becomes Fulfilled, every session of the patient ends, login with the old credentials gets the standard "Invalid email or password" result (FR-001 REQ-001-065), and the email address is free for a new registration, which creates a new account with no link to the old data (FR-001 REQ-001-182).

nodes.title: FR-024 drafts are not patient records; a discarded draft is soft-deleted and the discard is audited

attrs.statement: Treatment and package drafts of FR-024 hold no patient data and are not patient records, so a deletion request never touches them. A discarded draft follows the platform soft-delete rule (REQ-SYS-003): it is removed from every list and archived, and the discard is kept in the audit log (FR-024 REQ-024-022, REQ-023-011).

nodes.title: Admins create treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to create treatments with name, type, description, video, images, and technique specifications
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1008).

nodes.title: Admin edits create new treatment versions

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to edit existing treatments, creating new versions without modifying historical records
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1009).

nodes.title: Admin activates or deactivates treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to activate or deactivate treatments, affecting availability for new quotes and draft quotes only; sent quotes and bookings are not affected. Deactivate is offered only on Active treatments; an Inactive treatment is reactivated through Edit, which is versioned and sends the notice of REQ-024-042 when the treatment has been Active before, or of REQ-024-041 when it has never been Active; Draft and Pending Media Upload treatments have no Deactivate action.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; Alternative Flows A1 and A2; Screen 1 business rules.

nodes.title: Providers view active treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to view all active treatments from admin catalog
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1011).

nodes.title: Providers configure treatment pricing

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to configure pricing for treatments they want to offer (base price, price per graft, graft ranges)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1012).

nodes.title: Providers enable or disable offerings without losing pricing

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to enable or disable treatment offerings without deleting pricing configuration; a treatment pricing configuration is Not Offered until the provider sets it to Offered. Switching to Not Offered blocks new quotes for that treatment, leaves existing drafts and sent quotes unchanged, and a draft can still be sent.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 Status Toggle and business rules; Core Requirements.

nodes.title: Providers create packages

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to create packages with name, description, included items, included travel services, relative-day treatment plan, standard price, images, and status (Draft, Active, or Inactive); Draft applies only to a package that has no version yet.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; Main Flow: Provider Creates Package step 10; Screen 5 Status.

nodes.title: Package edit creates a new version

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to edit existing packages in the package library; each successful Update of an Active or Inactive package MUST create a new package version (v1, v2, and so on), keep earlier versions read-only, and never change existing quotes. Auto-save overwrites the working draft and creates no version, and neither the Deactivate button nor the bulk Deactivate creates one; setting Inactive on the edit form is an Update and creates a version.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; Alternative Flow A4 step 7; Screen 5 business rules.

nodes.title: Providers deactivate packages

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to deactivate packages, hiding them from new quotes while preserving existing quotes; Deactivate is offered only on Active packages, and an Inactive package is reactivated through Edit.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; Alternative Flow A5; Screen 4 business rules.

nodes.title: Treatment records are versioned and immutable

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain versioned treatment records with immutable history (no update-in-place of content); each successful Update Treatment creates a version, and Deactivate changes the status without creating one.
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; General Module Rule 3.

nodes.title: Package records are versioned and immutable

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain versioned package records with immutable history, including each version's included items, travel services, and relative-day plan
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1029).

nodes.title: Media stored in object storage with CDN delivery

attrs.statement: System MUST store media files (videos, images) in S3-compatible object storage with CDN delivery
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1030).

nodes.title: Track which providers offer which treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST track which providers offer which treatments (provider-treatment pricing configuration)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1031).

nodes.title: Packages are owned by a provider account

attrs.statement: System MUST link packages to provider accounts (package ownership)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1032).

nodes.title: Historical quotes and bookings keep exact versions

attrs.statement: System MUST preserve the exact Treatment version and Quote Option package snapshots used in historical quotes and bookings
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1033).

nodes.title: Only admins create or edit treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST restrict treatment creation/editing to admin users only
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1037).

nodes.title: Providers manage only their own packages

attrs.statement: System MUST restrict package management to provider users (edit only their own packages)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1038).

nodes.title: Media served over TLS 1.3 through CDN

attrs.statement: System MUST serve media files via CDN over TLS 1.3 (HTTPS)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1039).

nodes.title: Treatment and package changes are audit-logged

attrs.statement: System MUST log all treatment and package modifications with timestamp, user ID, IP address, and old/new values
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1040).

nodes.title: Uploaded media validated for type, size and malware

attrs.statement: System MUST validate uploaded media files for type, size, and malicious content
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1041).

nodes.title: Providers cannot see other providers' packages

attrs.statement: System MUST prevent providers from viewing other providers' package catalogs
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1042).

nodes.title: REST API for treatment CRUD, admin only

attrs.statement: System MUST expose REST API for treatment CRUD operations (admin access only)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1046).

nodes.title: REST API for packages with no hard delete

attrs.statement: System MUST expose REST API for package create, read, update (new version), and deactivate operations, with no hard delete (provider access only)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1047).

nodes.title: Integration with media storage service

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with S-05: Media Storage Service for video and image uploads
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1048).

nodes.title: Integration with CDN service

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with CDN service for media file delivery
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1049).

nodes.title: Integration with quote management for selection

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with PR-02: Inquiry & Quote Management for treatment and package selection during quote creation
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1050).

nodes.title: One system quote currency for all library prices

attrs.statement: System MUST use the system quote currency for all treatment and package library prices; providers MUST NOT choose a currency per treatment or package
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 944).

nodes.title: Packages are never hard-deleted

attrs.statement: System MUST NOT hard-delete packages; packages are deactivated or archived only
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 1021).

nodes.title: Treatment base price is reference only

attrs.statement: System MUST treat the provider treatment Base Price as a reference-only, non-binding value. It is not the clinic starting price: a clinic starting price is the lowest standard price among its active packages. Base Price MUST NOT be binding and MUST NOT be read after a quote is sent. Whether it prefills a new quote price row is owned by FR-004 (REQ-004-044)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary; Screen 3 rules; Key Entities.

nodes.title: Patients only view treatment and package content

attrs.statement: Patients view treatment details (videos, descriptions, technique information) and each provider's package-based quote options within provider quotes, shown from the quote option's own copy, and compare offerings across provider quotes. Patients have no direct treatment or package management actions.
attrs.rationale: Stated in Multi-Tenant Breakdown, Patient Platform (PRD lines 33-36) and Patient Entry Points (View-Only).

nodes.title: Entry points to treatment and package management

attrs.statement: Admin reaches treatment management from "Settings > Treatment Settings" ("Create New Treatment", or edit from the treatment list), and opens the treatment type list, the read-only provider packages view and the aftercare templates from the same treatment settings area. Provider reaches treatment pricing from "Products & Services > Treatments" ("Treatment Pricing") and the package catalog from "Products & Services > Packages" ("Create Package"). During quote creation the provider selects a treatment and one to five Active packages. Patients have view-only access through provider quotes.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points; User Story 1 scenario 3.

nodes.title: Treatments are one global catalog managed by admin

attrs.statement: All treatments are globally managed by admin and available to all active providers.
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, General Module Rule 1 (PRD line 600).

nodes.title: Admin can add new treatment types

attrs.statement: Admins maintain the treatment types (initially FUE, FUT, DHI, Sapphire FUE, Robotic, Other) as a managed list on the Admin Treatment Types screen; admins add new types and edit type names with no code change, and the Treatment Type field on Screens 1 and 2 chooses from exactly this list.
attrs.rationale: Module Scope (Admin Platform); Screen 6; Admin Editability Rules.

nodes.title: Admin views provider packages read-only for support

attrs.statement: Admin can view provider packages in read-only mode for support purposes only and cannot modify individual provider packages; provider ownership is enforced. The view lists only Active and Inactive packages, because a package draft is visible only to the provider's own team. View Details shows the full package version content (included items, travel services, plan, images, terms) read-only.
attrs.rationale: Module Scope (Admin Platform); Screen 7 purpose and business rules; Privacy Rule 2.

nodes.title: First time a treatment becomes Active: all active providers notified

attrs.statement: The first time a treatment becomes Active, by any route (saved as Active, an edit that activates a Draft or a never-Active Inactive treatment, or a media upload retry that ends Active), System sends all active providers the notification "New treatment available in catalog", and providers can then configure pricing for it. A treatment saved as Draft or Inactive sends nothing until it first becomes Active. System records on the treatment that it has been Active.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure; Main Flow: Admin Creates Treatment step 14; Alternative Flows A1 step 9 and B2 step 7.

nodes.title: Treatment update: providers who offer it notified

attrs.statement: When an admin updates a treatment that is Active after the save, System notifies the providers who currently offer that treatment about the update (for example "Treatment [FUE] video has been updated"). An edit of a Draft, Inactive, or Pending Media Upload treatment sends no update notice. When the update switches an Inactive treatment that has been Active before back to Active, the notice reads "treatment available again" and goes only to providers that have a pricing configuration for it; a treatment that has never been Active follows REQ-024-041 instead; the same treatment-updated event is used and no new event is added.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure; Alternative Flow A1 step 9; User Story 5.

nodes.title: Treatment deactivation: providers notified

attrs.statement: When an admin deactivates a treatment, by the Deactivate button or by setting Inactive on the edit form, System notifies the providers who offer the treatment with the message "Treatment [Name] has been deactivated".
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure and Alternative Flow A2 step 8.

nodes.title: Provider gets a confirmation after saving packages and pricing

attrs.statement: Provider receives a confirmation when a package is created or updated ("Package created successfully", "Package saved successfully") and when treatment pricing is saved ("Treatment pricing saved successfully").
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure (PRD line 70); Main Flow: Provider Creates Package step 15 (line 246); Screen 3 notes (line 436); Screen 5 notes (line 522).

nodes.title: Treatment media formats and size limits

attrs.statement: A treatment video is optional, MP4 only, max 50MB. Treatment images are optional, JPEG or PNG, max 5 images of 5MB each. Educational resources are optional PDF documents, max 3 files of 10MB each. These limits and formats are fixed in the code, not admin-editable. A video over the limit is rejected with "Video file exceeds maximum size of 50MB. Please compress the video or upload a shorter version."
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 5-7 (PRD lines 122-124); Screen 2 fields (lines 370-372); Admin Editability, Fixed in Codebase (lines 572-574); Edge Cases (line 912); validation example B1 (lines 197-199).

nodes.title: Treatment save validates inputs and shows errors on the field

attrs.statement: On Save Treatment, System validates name uniqueness, required fields (name, type, description) and file formats. The name is unique across all treatments, max 100 characters. Description max 5,000 characters, technique specifications max 2,000, expected recovery time max 50, typical duration 0.5 to 12 hours. Errors are shown next to the invalid fields and the treatment is created only after validation passes.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 10 (PRD line 127); B1 (lines 188-206); Screen 2 fields and rules (lines 356-377).

nodes.title: Treatment status is set by admin; only Active ones are visible to providers

attrs.statement: A treatment's status is Draft, Active, Inactive, or Pending Media Upload. The admin chooses Active or Inactive on save (default Active); Draft is set by Save as Draft, only for a treatment never saved as Active or Inactive; Pending Media Upload is set by the system when a media upload fails. Only Active treatments are visible to providers; Inactive, Draft and Pending Media Upload treatments are hidden from provider view.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow: Admin Creates Treatment steps 8 and 13; Screen 2 Status; Screen 3 rules.

nodes.title: Failed media upload retries, then saves without media

attrs.statement: When a media upload to S-05 fails (a video, an image, or an educational PDF), System retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If all retries fail it shows an error ("Media upload failed, please try again"), saves the treatment record without media marked "Pending Media Upload", stores the status the admin chose on the form (Active, Inactive, or Draft) with the record, and the admin can retry the upload separately by editing the treatment, or save the form again without the failed file; once the upload succeeds or the failed file is dropped the record leaves Pending Media Upload. Providers do not see or use a treatment in Pending Media Upload status until media is added. If an upload fails while any treatment is being edited, the edit is not saved: the previous saved media and status stay as they were (an Active treatment's previous version stays live) and the failed file is reported to the admin.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2; Edge Cases (media upload failure).

nodes.title: Treatment deactivation warns and needs admin confirmation

attrs.statement: Before a treatment becomes Inactive, by the Deactivate button or by setting Inactive on the edit form, System checks the open quotes (draft or sent) and the open FR-006 bookings (Accepted, Confirmed, In Progress, Aftercare) that use it, shows a warning with the number of providers offering it (Offered configurations of Active providers, the Number of Providers count), of active quotes, and of open bookings, and requires the admin to confirm; on confirmation the status becomes Inactive.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2 steps 1-6; Screen 1 business rules.

nodes.title: Deactivated treatment cannot be picked for new quotes

attrs.statement: Providers cannot select a deactivated treatment (Inactive by any route) in new quotes. If a treatment is deactivated while a provider has a draft quote open, System refreshes the available treatments and warns "Treatment [Name] is no longer available. Please select a different treatment." Sent quotes and bookings using the treatment keep the treatment version they recorded and continue unaffected; a draft quote that uses it must pick another treatment before it can be sent.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2 steps 7 and 9; Edge Cases; General Module Rule 4.

nodes.title: Treatments and packages are archived, never deleted; retention follows FR-023

attrs.statement: Treatments cannot be deleted: admins deactivate them (soft delete only). Deactivated treatments and packages are archived, not deleted, with the retention period governed by FR-023.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability, Configurable with Restrictions (PRD line 581); Data & Privacy Rules, Data Retention (line 561). REQ-024-033 covers packages never being hard-deleted.

nodes.title: Admin treatment list: order, search, filter, edit

attrs.statement: The admin treatment list shows Active treatments first, then Pending Media Upload, then Draft, with Inactive last; filters by treatment name in real time and by treatment type; shows "Create New Treatment" at all times; shows Deactivate only on Active treatments and Discard Draft only on Draft treatments; allows Edit on every treatment regardless of status; and shows 20 treatments per page.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules and notes.

nodes.title: Number of Providers counts providers offering the treatment

attrs.statement: Number of Providers on the admin treatment list is the count of provider treatment pricing configurations for that treatment whose status is Offered and whose provider account is Active. It is calculated, not entered; the treatment deactivation warning uses the same count.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 Number of Providers; Field Calculation Rules.

nodes.title: Timestamps shown in local timezone; Last Updated is updated_at

attrs.statement: All timestamps are displayed in the user's local timezone. Last Updated on every screen is the database updated_at timestamp, displayed in the user's local timezone.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 6 and Field Calculation Rules.

nodes.title: Draft auto-save and Cancel on the treatment and package forms

attrs.statement: The admin treatment form and the package form each auto-save a draft every 30 seconds to prevent data loss and offer Save as Draft. A saved draft has status Draft: a treatment draft is visible to admins only; a package draft is visible only to the provider's own team and cannot be selected in a quote. Status Draft applies to a treatment only while it has never been saved as Active or Inactive, and to a package only while it has no version. On a treatment already saved as Active or Inactive, or a package that has a version, auto-save and Save as Draft keep a working draft and change neither the live version nor the status until Update. Auto-save overwrites the working draft and creates no version. A draft needs a name to be saved. Cancel on either form discards unsaved changes and returns to the list. The admin who created a treatment draft, or the provider team that owns a package draft, can discard a draft that was never saved as Active or Inactive; the draft is removed and the removal is audited (REQ-024-022).
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 and Screen 5 rules and notes; Main Flow step 8; Provider package flow step 10.

nodes.title: Providers see active treatments and a Not Configured badge

attrs.statement: Providers can only view active treatments from the admin catalog. A treatment the provider has not configured pricing for shows a "Not Configured" badge, and treatments not yet configured are highlighted with a banner at the top of the screen.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 490-492, 506 (Screen 3 business rules and notes); line 174 (A3 step 2)

nodes.title: Pricing must be configured before a treatment is offered in quotes

attrs.statement: A provider must set a base price to enable "Offered" status and must configure pricing for a treatment before offering it in quotes. Saving the pricing configuration stores it; the treatment is available in quote creation only while the configuration status is Offered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 rules; Alternative Flow A3 steps 5 and 9.

nodes.title: Treatment pricing validation

attrs.statement: System validates treatment pricing on save: no negative values; base price > 0; price per graft optional and >= 0 (some treatments are fixed price, not graft-based); minimum graft count > 0 and below the maximum; maximum graft count greater than minimum. A maximum below the minimum shows "Maximum graft count must be greater than minimum graft count." next to the maximum field.
attrs.rationale: A3 step 7 (PRD line 182); Screen 3 fields and rules (lines 416-419, 427); Edge Cases (line 916).

nodes.title: Providers set their own prices without admin approval

attrs.statement: Providers have authority to set their own treatment pricing and package prices without admin approval.
attrs.rationale: Business Process Assumption 2 (PRD line 831), promoted because it states who decides prices.

nodes.title: Quick Copy Pricing between treatments

attrs.statement: Provider can copy a treatment's pricing configuration from another treatment with the "Quick Copy Pricing" option.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 notes (PRD line 505).

nodes.title: Package item types and travel services are fixed value lists

attrs.statement: Each included package item has a service type (medical, travel, accommodation, transport, flight, or other), a name, an optional description, an optional component price (>= 0), and an included flag. The service types are fixed in the code, aligned with FR-004. Included travel services are chosen from flight, hotel, transport, and other travel services.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow: Provider Creates Package steps 5-6 (PRD lines 236-237); Screen 5 fields (lines 491-492); Admin Editability, Fixed in Codebase (line 577).

nodes.title: Package plan uses relative days from Day 1

attrs.statement: A package's treatment plan uses relative days (Day 1, Day 2, and so on), each with a description, consecutive from Day 1; it never holds calendar dates.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 7 and step 12 (PRD lines 240, 245); Screen 5 field (line 493).

nodes.title: Package save validates inputs

attrs.statement: On Save Package, System validates: name not empty (max 100); description required (max 2,000); standard price > 0 with up to 2 decimal places; at least one included item with an allowed service type and component price >= 0; plan days consecutive from Day 1 with a description; duration max 50 characters in common patterns ("X nights", "X days", "X hours", "X sessions"); terms max 1,000 characters. Errors are shown next to the invalid fields and the package is created only after validation passes. The quick price edit on the package list applies the same price rule (above 0, up to 2 decimals).
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 12 (PRD line 243); B3 (lines 299-313); Screen 5 fields and rules (lines 488-505).

nodes.title: Package image formats and size limits

attrs.statement: Package images are optional, JPEG or PNG, max 3 images of 2MB each. The 2MB per-image limit is fixed in the code and not editable by providers. An image over the limit is rejected.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 8 (PRD line 239); Screen 5 field (line 496); Provider Editability, Fixed in Codebase (line 598); B3 (line 303).

nodes.title: Package name unique within the provider's catalog

attrs.statement: A package name must be unique within the provider's own package catalog and may repeat across providers. A duplicate name is rejected with "A package with this name already exists. Please choose a different name or edit the existing package."
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 rules (PRD line 503); Edge Cases (line 914).

nodes.title: A new package is version 1 and an Active one is selectable at once

attrs.statement: System saves a new package as version 1, linked to the provider account; a draft has no version until it is first saved as Active or Inactive. Whether it can be used in quote creation follows FR-004: only an Active package can be selected.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow: Provider Creates Package steps 14 and 16; Screen 5 rules.

nodes.title: New quote options copy the latest package version

attrs.statement: New quote options copy the latest version of the package.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A4 step 10 (PRD line 270).

nodes.title: No save-for-future from an inline package edit

attrs.statement: There is no "save for future" action from an inline package edit during quote creation. To reuse a change, the provider repeats it as a library edit in package management.
attrs.rationale: Package Edit Paths (PRD line 622).

nodes.title: Package deactivation warns of open quotes and needs confirmation

attrs.statement: Before a package becomes Inactive, by any route (Deactivate, setting the status to Inactive on the edit form, or the bulk Deactivate Selected), System counts the open quotes (draft or sent) that contain a quote option copied from the package, warns "This package is used in N open quotes. Deactivating hides it from new quotes; existing quotes are not changed.", and requires the provider to confirm; if the package is used in open quotes, confirmation is required. The bulk action shows one combined count and asks for one confirmation. On confirmation the status becomes Inactive. The Deactivate button and the bulk action create no version; on the edit form the same Update saves the new version with the status Inactive.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flows A4 step 5, A5 steps 3-6 and A11; Screen 4 and Screen 5 rules; User Story 6.

nodes.title: Provider can clone a package

attrs.statement: Provider can clone an existing package. System creates a new package record copied from the original with "(Copy)" appended to the name; the provider edits the name, duration, and price and saves it. Saving a clone counts as a new record toward the package creation limit.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A6; Screen 4 rules; Admin Editability Rules.

nodes.title: Usage Count of open quote options

attrs.statement: Usage Count on the package list is the number of FR-004 quote options copied from any version of the package whose parent quote is still open (status draft or sent). The deactivation warning shows the number of distinct open parent quotes among them. It is calculated, not entered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 field (PRD line 456) and rule (line 468); Field Calculation Rules (line 630).

nodes.title: Included Items summary shows first three items

attrs.statement: The package list shows a short summary of the included items: the first 3 items and "+N more". It is calculated, not entered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 field Included Items (PRD line 451).

nodes.title: Provider package list: order, search, filter, sort

attrs.statement: The provider package list shows Active packages first, then Draft packages, and Inactive last, shows Discard Draft only on a Draft package, filters by package name in real time and by status, can be sorted by name, price, or usage count, shows "Create New Package" at all times, and shows 20 packages per page.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and notes (PRD lines 462-469, 476).

nodes.title: Bulk actions and quick price edit on the package list

attrs.statement: The package list offers the bulk actions "Deactivate Selected" (one combined count of open quotes and one confirmation) and "Export to CSV". A quick price edit from the list (a pencil icon shows on hover, except on a Draft package, which has no version yet) is a library edit that applies the price rule of REQ-024-065 and saves a new package version.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 notes; Alternative Flow A11.

nodes.title: No platform limit on packages per provider

attrs.statement: There is no total limit on how many packages a provider can create; package creation is limited to 50 per hour per provider by default (admin setting). A new package counts once, when it is first saved as Active or Inactive (Save Package, including a clone); saving as a draft, auto-save, edits, and media upload retries do not count. When the limit is reached the save is refused with "You have reached the limit of [N] new packages per hour. Please try again later.", where N is the setting value.
attrs.rationale: Provider Editability Rules; Admin Editability Rules.

nodes.title: Package images only to patients viewing that provider's quote

attrs.statement: Package images are accessible only to patients viewing quotes from that provider, and are resolved from the package version recorded on the quote option.
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules, Privacy Rule 4 (PRD line 629).

nodes.title: Treatment media served by time-limited signed URLs

attrs.statement: Treatment videos and images are served via CDN using time-limited, signed URLs; unauthenticated bulk access is not allowed.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 628, 782 (Privacy Rule 3 signed URLs; CDN failure handling: no fallback to direct S3 URLs)

nodes.title: Library text and labels use translation keys; package free text follows the free-text switch

attrs.statement: Admin-authored library text (treatment descriptions and technique specifications) and all UI labels and error messages use FR-021 translation keys; FR-021 holds a treatment-library key group for the admin-authored text. The Screen 2 treatment form is the authoring screen for the English text: saving it writes the key's English source value (creating the key if new) and marks the dependent translations Review Needed; translation and publish stay in FR-021 (REQ-021-127). Provider-authored package names and descriptions are free text: they are shown as written, and machine-translated for the reader only when the FR-021 free-text translation switch is on (REQ-021-119). Treatment type codes (FUE, FUT, DHI, Sapphire FUE, Robotic), package item service type codes, and media file names and CDN URLs stay in English. Before production release all keyed treatment and package strings must be registered with the FR-021 translation management system.
attrs.rationale: Localization Rules; Dependencies, FR-021.

nodes.title: Provider staff role permissions gate package and pricing actions

attrs.statement: Role-based permissions (FR-009) determine which provider staff can use these actions: package create, edit, clone, deactivate, quick price edit, and treatment pricing configuration; each is permission-checked by staff role. The permission matrix is owned by FR-009 and FR-031.
attrs.rationale: Internal Dependencies, FR-009; Provider Editability Rules.

nodes.title: Package selection blocked when the package API is unavailable

attrs.statement: If the package API is temporarily unavailable, package selection is blocked with a retry message. System never seeds a quote option from cached data whose price or content does not match the package version it records.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Integration 3 error handling (PRD line 864), promoted because it is a business rule inside a technical section.

nodes.title: Package erasure and export follow FR-023 and GDPR

attrs.statement: EU providers can export their package data (GDPR). Package erasure requests follow FR-023 retention rules because quote history references package versions.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Security Considerations, Compliance (PRD line 881), promoted because it states an erasure and export obligation.

nodes.title: Admin edits medication and post-op instruction templates

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to manage the medication templates (common post-op medication presets that speed up prescribing) and the post-op instruction templates (standard instruction text that providers can customize). The medication templates are the one admin medication list providers pick medication from; the FR-011 medication catalogue is this same list. Each template is Active or Inactive; an admin can Deactivate and Reactivate it, an Inactive template is not offered to providers, and prescriptions and plans already given keep a copy of their text, so an edit or a change of status affects only future use
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary and Screen 8 (Admin Aftercare Templates).

nodes.title: Treatment card hover preview

attrs.statement: Each treatment on the admin treatment list shows its video thumbnail as a preview; hovering over the thumbnail plays a 3-second preview of the video.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 352 (Screen 1 notes: video thumbnail preview, hover plays 3 seconds)

nodes.title: Deactivation warning icon on treatment list

attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 353 (Screen 1 notes: warning icon next to treatments used in active quotes)

nodes.title: Treatment video upload progress and resume

attrs.statement: Treatment video upload shows a progress bar and supports resuming the upload after a failure.

nodes.title: Image upload by drag-and-drop or browse

nodes.title: Markdown editor with preview pane

attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 383, 390, 579 (Screen 2 and Screen 5 business rules and notes)

nodes.title: Inline video preview after upload

attrs.statement: After a treatment video is uploaded, the treatment form shows an inline video player preview.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 391 (Screen 2 notes)

nodes.title: Image thumbnails with remove option

attrs.statement: After upload, treatment images and package images are shown as thumbnails with a remove option; package image thumbnails can also be reordered.

nodes.title: Technique specifications tooltips

attrs.statement: The treatment form shows tooltips that explain the format of the technique specifications.

nodes.title: Expandable treatment cards with inline video

attrs.statement: Treatments on the provider treatment pricing screen are shown as cards that expand and collapse to show the full description; the treatment video plays inline when a card is expanded.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 479, 503-504 (Screen 3 description field and notes)

nodes.title: Save becomes Update when editing pricing

attrs.statement: On the provider treatment pricing screen the Save button becomes an Update button when the provider edits an existing pricing configuration.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 507 (Screen 3 notes)

nodes.title: Package form starter examples

attrs.statement: The package form offers starter examples, for example "Standard FUE with 5-night hotel and airport transfers".
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 587 (Screen 5 notes)

nodes.title: Package description character count

attrs.statement: The package form shows a character count for the description field.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 590 (Screen 5 notes)

nodes.title: Treatment creation rate limit

attrs.statement: Treatment creation is limited to 10 per hour per admin by default; the limit is an admin setting and a whole number of 1 or more. A new treatment counts once, when it is first saved as Active or Inactive (Save Treatment); saving as a draft, auto-save, edits, and media upload retries do not count. When the limit is reached the save is refused with "You have reached the limit of [N] new treatments per hour. Please try again later.", where N is the setting value.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules; Security Considerations threat mitigation.

nodes.title: Placeholder image when media fails to load

attrs.statement: When a treatment video or image fails to load from the CDN, the app shows a placeholder image; there is no fallback to direct S3 URLs.
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 782 (External Dependencies, CDN failure handling)

nodes.title: Chosen status stored and restored after a media upload retry

attrs.statement: The status the admin chose on the form (Active, Inactive, or Draft) is stored with a treatment record saved as Pending Media Upload and restored when a media upload retry succeeds or the form is saved again without the failed file; the same applies to an image or an educational PDF.
attrs.rationale: Edge Cases (media upload failure); Alternative Flow B2.

nodes.title: A package is not tied to a treatment

attrs.statement: A package is not tied to a treatment: a provider may use any of its Active packages with any treatment it offers. FR-004 owns how a quote picks the treatment and its packages.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 12 and Core Requirements; owner ruling on package and treatment independence.

nodes.title: Context types are fixed in code

attrs.statement: Context types are system-defined (fixed in source code). Admins cannot create, rename or delete context types; they assign one to each questionnaire set they create. Changes to context type definitions require a code deployment.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 rule (line 419): Admins cannot create, rename, or delete context types; changes to context type definitions require a code deployment

nodes.title: Context Type Reference screen is read-only

attrs.statement: This screen is entirely read-only; no fields are editable
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 427 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Set carries a required Context Type and optional tags

attrs.statement: Each questionnaire set carries a required Context Type and optional tags (e.g., "pain", "sleep", "compliance"). Downstream modules filter the catalog by compatible Context Type when presenting assignment options.
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 45 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Question context is inherited from its set

attrs.statement: System checks the parent set's Context Type (inherited — not chosen per question).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 flow diagram, question configuration step.

nodes.title: Set is a named, versioned package with one Context Type

attrs.statement: Each questionnaire set is a named, versioned package of questions with a single Context Type
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 502 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Publish needs at least one Active question

nodes.title: Questions are ordered; order sets display sequence

attrs.statement: Questions within a set are ordered; order determines display sequence to patients
attrs.rationale: Also: Question order must be maintained during updates

nodes.title: Duplicate set creates an independent Draft copy

attrs.statement: Duplicating a set creates a Draft copy with all questions, named `<source name> (copy)`; the Admin makes the name unique before the first save; the copy's Context Type is editable before first publish; the copy does not inherit the Inquiry designation
attrs.rationale: Business Rules 1 (line 496): A set may be duplicated to create a new Draft copy; the copy is independent of the source

nodes.title: Drag-and-drop reorder saves as Draft change

nodes.title: Question types are system-defined

attrs.statement: Question types are system-defined (fixed in source code); admin selects from the available type list but cannot create, rename, or remove types
attrs.rationale: Available system-defined types: Yes/No, Visual Scale 1–10, Numeric Scale 1–10, Multi-select, Free Text

nodes.title: Question Type locked after first save

attrs.statement: Question Type is locked after first save; changing type requires deleting and recreating the question
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 rule (line 362): Question Type is locked after first save; a confirmation dialog warns the admin before saving for the first time

nodes.title: Inquiry and Multi-Context questions need severity flag and Yes detail prompt

attrs.statement: Questions in Inquiry or Multi-Context sets: Severity Flag is required; Yes-answer detail prompt is required for Yes/No questions
attrs.rationale: Screen 3: Severity Flag and Alert Description are shown only if the parent set's Context Type is Inquiry or Multi-Context (line 355); Detail Prompt is required for Yes/No questions in those sets.

nodes.title: Publish blocked without a severity flag on every question

attrs.statement: All Active questions in Inquiry/Multi-Context sets must have a Severity flag before publishing
attrs.rationale: Severity flags must be assigned to all questions in Inquiry and Multi-Context sets Workflow 2: System enforces all questions in the set have a Severity Flag; blocks publish if any question is missing a flag.

nodes.title: MVP: Inquiry and Multi-Context sets are Yes/No only

attrs.statement: MVP: Inquiry and Multi-Context sets MUST contain only Yes/No questions; the system blocks publishing if any non-Yes/No questions exist
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 (line 316): MVP: Inquiry/Multi-Context sets can contain only Yes/No question types (enforced at publish-time) Screen 3 type validation: if parent set Context Type is Inquiry or Multi-Context, only Yes/No is selectable. Context-type table: MVP Yes/No only (hard constraint).

nodes.title: Future: typed answers in Inquiry sets once FR-003 supports them

attrs.statement: Future (V2+): Once FR-003 supports typed answers, Inquiry/Multi-Context sets may allow additional question types (with a publish-time warning)
attrs.rationale: Context-type table: additional question types allowed only after FR-003 supports typed answers.

nodes.title: Aftercare-only sets have no severity flags or alerts

attrs.statement: Aftercare-only questionnaire sets do not have severity flags and do not generate inquiry-style alerts; they support all system-defined question types
attrs.rationale: Context-type table: Aftercare supports all system-defined types; no severity flags.

nodes.title: Severity flags drive provider alerts for inquiry only

attrs.statement: Severity flags drive the automatic provider alert system for the inquiry flow only. Severity Flag and Alert Description are shown only on questions in Inquiry or Multi-Context sets; Alert Description is optional and an Admin-only note shown in the editor and Preview, and providers see the question text; response colour-coding in the provider view follows each answer's own flag automatically with no extra configuration; Preview shows no overall tier
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 scope: severity flags and the provider alert system apply exclusively to Inquiry-context and Multi-Context sets.

nodes.title: Severity flag definitions

attrs.statement: Critical questions: High-risk conditions (HIV, hepatitis, blood disorders, heart conditions) Standard questions: Moderate concerns (allergies, medications, chronic conditions) No Alert questions: General health status, lifestyle factors
attrs.rationale: prd.md lines 521.

nodes.title: No delivery frequency at question level

attrs.statement: Questions in Aftercare or Multi-Context sets: no frequency setting at question level — delivery frequency is configured in FR-011 at the milestone assignment step
attrs.rationale: Repeated at lines 318, 358, 561 and 572: Delivery frequency (how often the patient is prompted to complete the questionnaire at a given milestone) is configured in FR-011 at the milestone assignment level — not in FR-025 at the question level Frequency is not a question-level field; it is not validated here

nodes.title: Conditional question fields follow the question type

attrs.statement: Conditional fields (Detail Prompt, Scale Labels, Options, Placeholder, Max Characters) are shown or hidden dynamically based on the selected Question Type. Type-specific fields follow the selected type: Visual Scale 1-10 requires a label for each scale point; Numeric Scale 1-10 requires minimum and maximum end labels; Multi-select requires at least 2 options; Free Text may have a placeholder text and an optional maximum character limit
attrs.rationale: Per-type requirements from the Screen 3 table: Scale Point Labels required for Visual Scale 1-10; Scale Min/Max Labels required for Numeric Scale 1-10; Options required for Multi-select (min 2 options); Placeholder Text and Max Characters optional for Free Text (Max Characters integer > 0).

nodes.title: Question text meets minimum length

attrs.statement: Question text must be at least 10 characters
attrs.rationale: Screen 3: Question Text min 10 chars.

nodes.title: Duplicate question text in a set is prevented

attrs.statement: Duplicate question text within the same set must be prevented
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 587 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: All questions pass completeness before publish

attrs.statement: All Active questions must pass completeness validation before the parent set can be published. Saving accepts an incomplete question and keeps its status; publish lists the incomplete questions, and the Admin completes them or sets them Inactive
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative flow A4: Incomplete questions found: System blocks publish and lists incomplete questions.

nodes.title: Category required before publish

attrs.statement: Every questionnaire set must be assigned a category before it can be published; the category must exist and be Active
attrs.rationale: The set must have a Category assigned before publishing A category must be assigned to the questionnaire set

nodes.title: Categories are global; one category per set

attrs.statement: Categories are global across all questionnaire sets
attrs.rationale: Each questionnaire set belongs to exactly one category Categories are used for organising and filtering the Questionnaire Catalog (Screen 1) Screen 4 (line 391): Each questionnaire set belongs to exactly one category

nodes.title: Category names are unique

attrs.statement: Category names must be unique
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 398 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: A category is deleted only when no set is assigned, otherwise it is deactivated

nodes.title: Category deactivation keeps assignments and flags sets Uncategorised

nodes.title: Category assignment consistent across catalog views

attrs.statement: Category assignment must be consistent across catalog views
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 593 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Publish increments version and archives previous Active

attrs.statement: Publishing increments the version number and archives the previous Active version; a designation of the set for Inquiry stays on the set and carries over to the new version
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 publish step: System increments version, marks set as Active; archives previous Active version.

nodes.title: Editing a published set creates a Draft; Active keeps serving

attrs.statement: Every change to an Active (published) set (add, edit, delete or reorder a question, metadata, Context Type) is saved to the set's single open Draft; the Active version continues to serve downstream consumers until the Draft is published; a set has at most one open Draft
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative flow A1 and Workflow 2 flow B1: the published Active version stays unchanged until the new Draft is published.

nodes.title: Context Type locked while set is Active

attrs.statement: Context Type is read-only on the Active version and editable only in an open Draft; publishing a Draft whose Context Type no longer fits a current use (Inquiry designation or milestone assignment) is blocked with the list of those uses
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 319 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Version activation needs explicit admin confirmation

attrs.statement: Version activation requires explicit admin confirmation, shown after validation with the new version number and changes summary
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 541 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Changes require admin authentication and authorization

attrs.statement: Changes require admin authentication and authorization
attrs.rationale: Security Considerations (line 665): Strict admin-only access to questionnaire management.

nodes.title: All question changes are version controlled

attrs.statement: All question changes must be version controlled
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 538 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Previous versions are archived, not deleted

attrs.statement: Previous versions must be archived, not deleted
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 540 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Earlier versions restorable as a new Draft, then published

attrs.statement: Any earlier version must be restorable as a new Draft, which is then published; there is no one-step rollback, and the Active version is unaffected until the restored Draft is published; Restore is refused while the set has an open Draft; on an Archived set the set shows status Draft from the restore until the restored Draft is published
attrs.rationale: Screen 7: "Restore as New Draft" creates a new Draft version of the set with the questions from the selected historical version; the currently Active version is not affected until the restored Draft is published

nodes.title: View Snapshot is read-only

attrs.statement: "View Snapshot" opens a read-only view of the questionnaire set at that version; no editing is possible from the snapshot view
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 495 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Version history and audit trail kept indefinitely and tamper-proof

attrs.statement: Version history and audit trail are maintained indefinitely and are tamper-proof
attrs.rationale: Audit logs must be retained for compliance requirements Audit trail must be tamper-proof and immutable

nodes.title: All admin actions on a set are audited

attrs.statement: All admin actions on the set — including metadata edits, question changes, duplicate, delete, reorder, designation changes, and publish/archive events — are captured in the audit trail, each with a timestamp and the identity of the admin
attrs.rationale: All changes must be logged with timestamp and admin identification

nodes.title: Audit entries hold before and after values

attrs.statement: Audit trail must include before/after values for all modifications
attrs.rationale: prd.md line 546 (found by matching the rule statement to the PRD text).

nodes.title: Audit entries track IP address and session
